# The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars

> [!abstract]
> 1. The Bible's later books describe, without naming anyone, a woman whose sign is a sun, a moon, and a crown of twelve stars (Revelation 12:1), twelve princes from Ishmael (Genesis 17:20), and a future king who judges the poor and fills the earth with justice and the knowledge of God (Isaiah 11:1-9, Psalm 72, Daniel 7:13-14).
> 2. The Qur'an swears by a sun and by a moon that follows it (Qur'an 91:1-2), and the Imams' transmitted tafsir names that sun as the Prophet ﷺ and that moon as Ali ﵇.
> 3. Shia and Sunni collections report twelve successors from Quraysh, the Musnad of Ahmad ties the number to the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel, and the Imami reports name twelve Imams, first Ali קּ and last the Mahdi, eleven of them Fatimah's כֿ descendants.
> 4. Both traditions report an end-time ruler from the Prophet's ﷺ progeny, and reports of both place the returning Isa קּ beside him rather than on his throne.
>
> The conclusion is a weighed reading. The Bible's unnamed figures and the Islamic corpus's named figures carry the same assignments, so the Bible carries the job description and the Islamic reports carry the names of those who fill it.

## No verse names the house

No verse of the Hebrew Bible or the New Testament names Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, or any Imam. Christians who expect a coming king read the same books and find Jesus ﵇ in them. A claim that the Bible contains the Prophet's family by name would be false, and the case made here does not rest on one.

What the Bible does contain is a set of unnamed figures defined by relations and by work. A woman stands clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars (Revelation 12:1). Ishmael is promised twelve princes and a great nation (Genesis 17:20). A future king from Jesse judges the poor with righteousness, kills the wicked, and fills the earth with the knowledge of God (Isaiah 11:1-9). The question here is narrow. Do the job descriptions the Bible assigns to its unnamed figures match the assignments the Islamic corpus itself makes, in its own reports, to the Prophet's house?

That question can be answered without forcing a single verse. The Qur'an swears by a sun and a moon, and the Imams' transmitted exegesis names that sun and that moon. The Prophet ﷺ is reported in Shia and Sunni collections alike to have counted twelve successors and to have tied that number to the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel. He is reported to have described an end-time ruler from Fatimah's ﵍ descendants who fills the earth with justice, and to have distinguished that ruler from the returning Isa ﵇. If those reports carry the Tradition's own assignment of the sky's lights to the Prophet's house, and its own count of twelve, then the Bible's woman, its twelve princes, and its reigning king describe a configuration the Islamic sources had already assembled under names.

A match of assignments is a reading, and a reading can be weighed. It is not a named prophecy, and it does not refute a Christian who assigns the same texts to a future advent of Jesus ﵇.

## A woman clothed with the sun

The twelfth chapter of Revelation begins with a sign in heaven.

> [!quote]- Revelation 12:1-2, Textus Receptus, Van Dyck, King James Version
> και σημειον μεγα ωφθη εν τω ουρανω γυνη περιβεβλημενη τον ηλιον και η σεληνη υποκατω των ποδων αυτης και επι της κεφαλης αυτης στεφανος αστερων δωδεκα και εν γαστρι εχουσα κραζει ωδινουσα και βασανιζομενη τεκειν
>
> 1 وظهرت آية عظيمة في السماء امرأته متسربلة بالشمس والقمر تحت رجليها وعلى رأسها إكليل من اثني عشر كوكبا . 2 وهي حبلى تصرخ متمخضة ومتوجعة لتلد .
>
> kai sēmeion mega ōphthē en tō ouranō, gunē peribeblēmenē ton hēlion, kai hē selēnē hupokatō tōn podōn autēs, kai epi tēs kephalēs autēs stephanos asterōn dōdeka, kai en gastri echousa kraizei, ōdinousa kai basanizomenē tekein.
>
> "And there appeared a great wonder in heaven; a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars: And she being with child cried, travailing in birth, and pained to be delivered."

Her child is caught up to God, and the war moves to the rest of her seed.

> [!quote]- Revelation 12:5, Textus Receptus, Van Dyck, King James Version
> και ετεκεν υιον αρρενα ος μελλει ποιμαινειν παντα τα εθνη εν ραβδω σιδηρα και ηρπασθη το τεκνον αυτης προς τον θεον και τον θρονον αυτου
>
> 5 فولدت ابنا ذكرا عتيدا أن يرعى جميع الأمم بعصا من حديد . واختطف ولدها إلى الله وإلى عرشه .
>
> kai eteken huion arrena, hos mellei poimainein panta ta ethnē en hrabdō sidērā, kai hērpasthē to teknon autēs pros ton theon kai ton thronon autou.
>
> "And she brought forth a man child, who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron: and her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne."

> [!quote]- Revelation 12:17, Textus Receptus, Van Dyck, King James Version
> και ωργισθη ο δρακων επι τη γυναικι και απηλθεν ποιησαι πολεμον μετα των λοιπων του σπερματος αυτης των τηρουντων τας εντολας του θεου και εχοντων την μαρτυριαν του ιησου χριστου
>
> 17 فغضب التنين على المرأة وذهب ليصنع حربا مع باقي نسلها الذين يحفظون وصايا الله وعندهم شهادة يسوع المسيح
>
> kai ōrgisthē ho drakōn epi tē gunaiki, kai apēlthen poiēsai polemon meta tōn loipōn tou spermatos autēs, tōn tērountōn tas entolas tou theou kai echontōn tēn marturian Iēsou christou.
>
> "And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ."

Three elements define the woman. She is associated with the sun, with the moon, and with exactly twelve stars. The dragon is identified within the chapter itself as Satan (Revelation 12:9), and the male child is the one destined to rule the nations. The passage does not name the woman, and readers have supplied the name for two thousand years.

## Who the churches say she is

Christian interpretation has never settled on one woman. Pope Pius XII, defining the Assumption of Mary in 1950, wrote that the scholastic doctors recognized the Assumption as signified in "that woman clothed with the sun whom John the Apostle contemplated on the Island of Patmos" (Munificentissimus Deus 27). The Catholic Encyclopedia's article on the Apocalypse states the historical-critical reading in one line. "The woman in travail is a personification of the synagogue or the church. Her first-born is Christ, her other seed is the community of the faithful" (Van den Biesen, "Apocalypse," 1907). The same article reads the imagery through Israel's own scriptures, noting the crown of twelve stars and the sun and moon under her feet with a cross-reference to Genesis 37:9-10, Joseph's dream.

The standard Christian identifications are Mary, the Church, and Israel, and the encyclopedia's own cross-reference sends the image back to Joseph's dream, in which the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 37:9). On the Israel reading the woman is Jacob's household and the sign retells the dream. That explains where the image came from. It does not settle who the woman is, and the chapter's war between her seed and the dragon still asks for her. None of these readings is a fact about the text. Each is an assignment, and the assignment has to fit the figure's relations. A woman whose sign is a sun she wears, a moon under her feet, and twelve stars as her crown is a woman set among those lights, and any reading of her names a household for them.

## An oath by the sun and the moon

The Qur'an opens the ninety-first sura with an oath.

> [!quote]- Qur'an 91:1-4, as cited in Ta'wil al-Ayat, vol. 2, p. 367
> قال الله تعالى : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والشمس وضحاها (1) والقمر إذا تلاها (2) والنهار إذا جلاها (3) والليل إذا يغشاها (4)
>
> Bismi llahi r-rahmani r-rahim. Wa-sh-shamsi wa-duhaha, wa-l-qamari idha talaha, wa-n-nahari idha jallaha, wa-l-layli idha yaghshaha.
>
> God, Most High, said, "In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the sun and its morning brightness (1), and by the moon when it follows it (2), and by the day when it reveals it (3), and by the night when it covers it (4)."

The verb of the oath is tala, to follow. Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi records the reading of the school with a full chain.

> [!info]- Imam al-Sadiq, Tafsir al-Qummi, vol. 2, p. 424
> سورة الشمس مكية آياتها خمس عشرة (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والشمس وضحاها) قال : أخبرني أبي عن سليمان الديلمي عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : سألته عن قول الله ﷿ والشمس وضحاها ، قال : الشمس رسول الله ﵌ أوضح الله به للناس دينهم قلت : (والقمر إذا تلاها) قال ذلك أمير المؤمنين (ع) قلت : (والليل إذا يغشاها) قال : ذلك أئمة الجور الذين استبدوا للامر دون آل رسول الله ﵌ وجلسوا مجلسا كان آل رسول الله ﵌ أولى به منهم ، فغشوا دين رسول الله ﵌ بالظلم والجور وهو قوله : والليل إذا يغشاها ، قال : يغشى ظلمهم ضوء النهار ، قلت : (والنهار إذا جلاها) قال : ذلك الامام من ذرية فاطمة ﵍ يسئل عن دين رسول الله فيجلى لمن يسأله ،
>
> Surat al-Shams is Meccan. Its verses are fifteen.
>
> In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. "By the sun and its morning brightness."
>
> He said, "My father informed me from Sulayman al-Daylami, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, 'I asked him about the saying of God, "By the sun and its morning brightness." He said, "The sun is the Messenger of God. Through him God made His religion clear to the people."
>
> I said, "And the moon when it follows it."
>
> He said, "That is the Commander of the Faithful."
>
> I said, "And the night when it covers it."
>
> He said, "Those are the imams of tyranny who seized authority apart from the family of the Messenger of God and occupied a position to which the family of the Messenger of God had a greater right than they did. They covered the religion of the Messenger of God with wrongdoing and tyranny. This is His saying, 'And the night when it covers it.' Their wrongdoing covers the light of day."
>
> I said, "And the day when it makes it clear."
>
> He said, "That is the imam from the descendants of Fatimah. He is asked about the religion of the Messenger of God, and he makes it clear for whoever asks him.'"

The sun is Muhammad ﷺ, through whom God made the religion clear. The moon that follows him is Ali ﵇. The night that covers is the seizure of rule from the family of the Messenger ﷺ. The day that reveals is an Imam from Fatimah's ﵍ descendants who answers questions about the Prophet's religion. Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi, who died in the fourth century, carries the same distribution from al-Husayn ﵇ himself.

> [!info]- Al-Husayn, Tafsir Furat al-Kufi, p. 563, report 721
> 721 - 3 فرات قال : حدثني علي بن محمد بن عمر الزهري معنعنا : عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال : قال الحارث [بن عبد الله] الأعور للحسين ﵇ : يا ابن رسول الله جعلت فداك أخبرني عن قول الله في كتابه : (والشمس وضحاها) قال : ويحك يا حارث ذلك محمد رسول الله ﵌ . قال : قلت : جعلت فداك : قوله : (والقمر إذا تلاها) قال : ذلك أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ يتلو محمدا ﵌ . قال : قلت : (والنهار إذا جلاها) قال : ذلك القائم من آل محمد ﵌ يملأ الأرض عدلا وقسطا .
>
> Furat said, "Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Umar al-Zuhri narrated to me, with a chain of transmission, from Abu Jafar, who said, 'Al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-Awar said to al-Husayn, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, may I be made your ransom, tell me about God's saying in His Book, 'By the sun and its brightness.'"
>
> He said, "Woe to you, Harith. That is Muhammad, the Messenger of God."
>
> He said, "I said, 'May I be made your ransom. His saying, 'And by the moon when it follows it.'"
>
> He said, "That is the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, following Muhammad."
>
> He said, "I said, 'And by the day when it reveals it.'"
>
> He said, "That is the Qa'im from the family of Muhammad. He will fill the earth with justice and equity."'"

The answer to the opening question is yes. In the Imami transmission the sun of the oath is the Prophet ﷺ and its moon is Ali ﵇, and the day is the Qa'im, the one who rises, who fills the earth with justice. The reading is not a single stray voice. Al-Kulayni's al-Kafi carries it in the Rawda volume, and al-Qummi and Furat carry it through independent chains, with Ibn Abbas versions beside them in Furat and Ibn Shahrashub. One recorded variant assigns the figures differently.

> [!warning]- Imam al-Sadiq, Ta'wil al-Ayat, vol. 2, pp. 367-368, minority channel
> لهذه تأويل ظاهر وباطن : فالظاهر ظاهر ، وأما الباطن فهو : 1 - ما رواه علي بن محمد ، عن أبي جميلة ، عن الحلبي . ورواه (أيضا) (1) علي بن الحكم ، عن أبان بن عثمان ، عن الفضل بن العباس عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ (أنه) (2) قال (والشمس وضحاها) الشمس : أمير المؤمنين ﵇ " وضحاها " قيام القائم (3) ﵇ (لان الله سبحانه قال (وأن يحشر الناس ضحى) (4) . (والقمر إذا تلاها) الحسن والحسين ﵉ . (والنهار إذا جلاها) هو قيام القائم ﵇ . (والليل إذا يغشاها) حبتر (ودولته قد غشى) (5) عليه الحق . وأما قوله (والسماء وما بناها) قال : هو محمد - عليه وآله السلام - هو السماء الذي يسموا إليه الخلف في العلم .
>
> This has an outward interpretation and an inward interpretation. The outward is outward. As for the inward interpretation, it is as follows.
>
> Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Jamilah, from al-Halabi. Ali ibn al-Hakam also narrated it from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "By the sun and its morning brightness. The sun is the Commander of the Faithful. Its morning brightness is the rising of the Qa'im, because God, exalted is He, said, 'And that the people will be gathered in the morning.' And the moon when it follows it refers to Hasan and Husayn."
>
> "And the day when it reveals it" is the rising of the Qa'im.
>
> "And the night when it covers it" is Habtar, and his rule has covered the truth.
>
> As for His saying, "And the heaven and He who built it," he said, "It is Muhammad. He is the heaven to which successors ascend in knowledge."

In this version the sun is Ali ﵇, the moon is al-Hasan and al-Husayn ﵈, and the heaven is Muhammad ﷺ. Sharaf al-Din al-Astarabadi, who collected it in Ta'wil al-Ayat, transmits it through two chains that converge on one report, the line of Abu Jamila from al-Halabi beside the line of Ali ibn al-Hakam, and al-Burhan and Bihar al-Anwar carry it from him rather than independently. The version that makes the sun the Prophet ﷺ and the moon Ali ﵇ is the one with the wider distribution in the early collections, in al-Kafi, al-Qummi, Furat, and Ibn Shahrashub's Manaqib. In the early transmission of the school, that is the reading of the oath the woman of Revelation 12 would need.

## The lights of one house

The reports do not leave the sun and the moon as a pair. Al-Saduq devotes a chapter of Ma'ani al-Akhbar to the question and gathers three chains to one report.

> [!note]- The Prophet, Ma'ani al-Akhbar, pp. 208-209, with three chains, p. 208
> (باب) * (معنى الشمس والقمر والزهرة والفرقدين) * 1 - حدثنا أبو الحسن محمد بن عمر [و] بن علي بن عبد الله البصري ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر عبد الله بن علي الكرخي ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثنا أبي قال : حدثنا عبد الرزاق الصنعاني ، قال : حدثنا معمر ، عن الزهري ، عن أنس بن مالك قال : صلى رسول الله ﵌ صلاة الفجر ، فلما انفتل من صلاته أقبل علينا بوجهه الكريم على الله ﷿ ثم قال : معاشر الناس من افتقد الشمس فليستمسك بالقمر ، ومن افتقد القمر فليستمسك بالزهرة ، فمن افتقد الزهرة فليستمسك (2) بالفرقدين . ثم قال رسول الله ﵌ : أنا الشمس ، وعلي القمر ، وفاطمة الزهرة ، والحسن والحسين الفرقدان . وكتاب الله لا يفترقان حتى يردا علي الحوض . - 2 حدثنا أبو الحسن محمد بن عمر [و] البصري ، قال : حدثنا أبو القاسم نصر بن الحسين الصفار النهاوندي بها ، قال : حدثنا أبو الفرج أحمد بن محمد بن خوزي السامري ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر القاسم بن إبراهيم القنطري ، قال : حدثنا إبراهيم بن خالد الحلواني ، قال حدثنا محمد بن خلف العسقلاني ، قال : حدثنا محمد بن السري ، عن محمد بن المنكدر ، عن جابر بن عبد الله ، قال . قال رسول الله ﵌ : اقتدوا بالشمس فإذا غابت الشمس فاقتدوا
>
> Chapter on the meaning of the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqads
>
> Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Basri narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Karkhi narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us. He said that his father narrated to us. He said that Abd al-Razzaq al-San'ani narrated to us from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said
>
> The Messenger of God performed the dawn prayer. When he had turned away after his prayer, he turned toward us with his noble face, God exalted be He, and said, "People, whoever loses the sun should hold fast to the moon. Whoever loses the moon should hold fast to Venus. Whoever loses Venus should hold fast to the two Farqads."
>
> Then the Messenger of God said, "I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Fatima is Venus, and Hasan and Husayn are the two Farqads. They and the Book of God will not separate until they come to me at the Pool."
>
> Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Umar al-Basri narrated to us. He said that Abu al-Qasim Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Saffar al-Nahawandi narrated to us there. He said that Abu al-Faraj Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khuwayzi al-Samiri narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim al-Qantari narrated to us. He said that Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Hulwani narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said
>
> The Messenger of God said, "Follow the sun. When the sun sets, follow"

> [!note]- The Prophet, Ma'ani al-Akhbar, pp. 208-209, with three chains, continued, p. 209
> بالقمر ، فإذا غاب القمر فاقتدوا بالزهرة فإذا غابت الزهرة فاقتدوا بالفرقدين فقالوا : يا رسول الله فما الشمس ؟ وما القمر ؟ وما الزهرة ؟ وما الفرقدان ؟ فقال : أنا الشمس ، وعلي القمر ، والزهرة فاطمة ، والفرقدان الحسن والحسين
>
> by the moon. When the moon disappears, follow Venus. When Venus disappears, follow the two Farqad stars." They said, "Messenger of God, what are the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqad stars?" He said, "I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Venus is Fatimah, and the two Farqad stars are Hasan and Husayn."

The five lights of the sky are the five of the house, and the report is not Shia property alone. Al-Safuri al-Shafi'i carries it in Nuzhat al-Majalis and names his source, al-Thalabi's Ara'is, and al-Natanzi carries it in al-Khasais.

> [!note]- The Prophet, Nuzhat al-Majalis, vol. 2, p. 315, citing al-Thalabi's Ara'is

The shining stars are the nine Imams from al-Husayn's ﵇ loins, the ninth their Mahdi, and the count is tied, in the Prophet's ﷺ own words as reported, to the twelve tribes of Yaqub and the twelve apostles of Isa ﵇. Count the figures. Revelation places a woman, a sun, a moon, and twelve stars in one sign. The code places the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqads over the Prophet ﷺ, Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, al-Hasan ﵇, and al-Husayn ﵇, and the shining stars over the nine Imams after al-Husayn ﵇. No report assigns the crown itself. The reports give the moon to Ali, the two Farqads to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and nine shining stars to the Imams after al-Husayn, while the Tablet family of reports counts the Imams as twelve. Reading Revelation's crown of twelve as those twelve Imams, with Ali among them beside his moon, is where the inference begins.

One qualification belongs here, because the obvious bridge from Joseph's dream to the Imams has no classical support. The Imam-side tafsirs of Qur'an 12:4 read Joseph's dream literally.

## The Fatimah reading and its history

> [!note]- Labib Baydun, Mawsu'at Karbala, vol. 1, p. 131
> 45 - الإنجيل يتنبّأ بالأئمة الاثني عشر : جاء في الإصحاح الحادي عشر عن تنبؤات يوحنا اللاهوتي ما نصه : « وظهرت آية عظيمة في السماء ، امرأة متسربلة بالشمس ، وتحت رجليها القمر ، وعلى رأسها إكليل من اثني عشر كوكبا » . فكأنه يتكلم عن مولاتنا فاطمة الزهراء ﵍ وقد تسربلت بالشمس يعني أبيها محمّد ﵌ ، وتزوجت بالقمر وهو علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وعلى رأسها إكليل من أبنائها المعصومين الاثني عشر ، الذين أولهم الحسن والحسين وآخرهم المهدي ﵇ . وليس هناك فيما تنبّأ به يوحنا اللاهوتي فيما سيحصل من أمور ، شيء شبيه بالذي ذكر ، غير فاطمة وأبيها وبعلها وبنيها ﵈ .
>
> The Gospel foretells the twelve Imams.
>
> In the eleventh chapter, the following occurs among the prophecies of John the Theologian.
>
> "A great sign appeared in heaven, a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars."
>
> It is as though he is speaking of our lady Fatima al-Zahra. She was clothed with the sun, meaning her father Muhammad, and married to the moon, who is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Upon her head is a crown from her twelve infallible sons, the first of whom are al-Hasan and al-Husayn and the last of whom is the Mahdi.
>
> Among what John the Theologian foretold would occur, there is nothing resembling what he mentioned except Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons.

The mapping is complete, woman, sun, moon, crown, and the encyclopedia's phrase about the sons strains the arithmetic by one, since eleven of the twelve descend from her and the count includes her husband. The full form, with the dragon and the child, appears in the earliest Imami carrier found, Ilzam al-Nasib of al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, written in the early fourteenth century AH. His rendering of the vision paraphrases loosely and folds in clauses about mountains lowered and rough places smoothed that Revelation itself does not carry; the exhibit keeps his text as it stands.

> [!tip]- Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, pp. 129-130, p. 129

>
> The seventeenth glad tiding concerning the support of the community is from the Revelations of John, in chapter twelve, verse one. Its translation is as follows. "A sign appeared in heaven. It was a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and a crown of twelve stars upon her head. While she was pregnant, behold, a serpent will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be lowered, the crooked places will be made straight, and the rough places will become smooth. Those stars are upon the earth, and the serpent stands before the woman who is pregnant and about to give birth, in order to take her child after she gives birth. So she gave birth to a sound male, who rules all the groups with an iron rod. He was carried away and taken to God, and reached His abode and throne." End.
>
> The author said, "What is meant by the woman is Fatimah al-Zahra, for her light surpassed the sun. The moon is beneath her foot, and she is higher and more majestic. Indeed, its light is one part of thousands of parts of portions of her light and is acquired from her. The crown containing the twelve constellations is the twelve Imams, peace be upon them all. What is meant by that serpent is the tree of Banu Umayyah, the wicked tree. It killed the shining spiritual stars. What is meant by the child is the hidden Imam, the Qa'im. Since the enemies wanted to kill him, he concealed himself and was veiled from sight. The iron rod is a metaphor for the sword. He will fight the groups upon the face of the earth with the sword, fill the earth with equity and justice, and the structure of unbelief, error, and oppression will vanish and collapse. Jesus the Messiah is not meant, because he never fought. Rather, the Messiah was a manifestation of mercy. It is possible that the twelve stars mean Muhammad, Ali, and ten of his sons, and that the moon is a metaphor for the Qa'im. It does not apply to Mary, Jesus, and the disciples, because although they were twelve, one of them apostatized, which conflicts with the known number."

> [!tip]- Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, pp. 129-130, continued, p. 130
> وما فسره بعض علماء النصارى من أن المراد من المرأة هي المعبد والكنيسة ، والنجوم الاثني عشر عبارة عن الحوراء الملازمة لها الحافات حولها ، وذلك حيث ذكر في الباب الثاني من المكاشفات أن اكتب للحوراء الموكلة بكنيسة أقس أن من بيده النجوم السبع يسير في المصابيح السبعة المذهبة ، ففيه أن الكنايس لا تشتمل على الحور ولا يناسب ذكر النجم لها أيضا وبعيد جدا ، والتعبير عن الخادم والحارث والحفظة مع ما هم عليه من الظلمة بالنورانية والبهاء أبعد خطأ عند العقلاء .
>
> What some Christian scholars interpreted is that the woman means the temple and the church, and that the twelve stars refer to the maidens attached to her and surrounding her. This is because chapter two of the Apocalypse mentions, "Write to the maiden appointed over the church of Ephesus, that He who holds the seven stars walks among the seven golden lampstands." Yet churches do not contain maidens, nor is it fitting to call her a star. This is very far-fetched. Moreover, to describe the servant, the cultivator, and the guards, despite their darkness, as luminous and radiant is an even more erroneous mistake in the judgment of rational people.

Al-Ha'iri reads the dragon as the tree of Banu Umayyah, the male child as the hidden Qa'im, and the iron rod as his sword, and he argues that the child cannot be Jesus ﵇ because Jesus ﵇ never fought. He records the Christian exegesis of his own day, which read the woman as the temple or the church, and rejects it, and he offers an alternative distribution of his own in which the twelve stars are Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇, and ten of his descendants and the moon is the Qa'im.

The provenance has a limit that matters. A corpus search for the woman of Revelation 12 across the classical Imami literature, al-Kafi, the tafsirs, Bihar al-Anwar in its hundred and more volumes, returns nothing before the modern period. The earliest explicit carrier found is Ilzam al-Nasib. The argumentative ancestry runs through Jawad ibn Ibrahim Sabat al-Hanafi, whose Revelation material later Imami authors recycled, and Milani's Nafahat al-Azhar carries that line in its eighteenth volume. The modern authors also disagree with one another. One makes the sun Ali ﵇ and the woman's travail her miscarriage of Muhsin, and one makes the woman Narjis, the Mahdi's mother, with the sun as Imam al-Hasan al-Askari ﵇. The reading of the woman as Fatimah ﵍, with her father as the sun and her husband as the moon, is the commonest modern form, and Mawsu'at Karbala states it in its cleanest shape. (The encyclopedia's chapter reference slips by one. The quotation is Revelation 12:1.)

The classical Imami corpus never reads Revelation 12, and the reading of it as Fatimah ﵍ is modern. The modern reading assembles elements the classical corpus had already transmitted, the sun as the Prophet ﷺ and the moon as Ali ﵇ in the exegesis of Qur'an 91, the nine shining stars as the Imams from al-Husayn's line in the Salman report, and the woman as the one whose father, husband, and descendants they are. The Bible supplies a sign whose elements are a sun, a moon, and twelve stars around one woman. The Islamic corpus supplies a house whose members carry exactly those signs. The connection between the two is a modern inference, and it stands here as one.

The interpretation of the blessing, al-Rawandi says, is Muhammad ﷺ. Majlisi, in the seventeenth century, records that he heard the Hebrew text from People of the Book he trusted.

Majlisi transliterates the received text and adds his own view that the blessing's "maddmad," the doubled word of the Hebrew, is the name Muhammad ﵇ in Hebrew. Bihar also carries a longer narrative in which Abraham is shown the twelve in a vision and told they will come forth "from your firstborn Ishmael."

So rejoice, Abraham. I shall join your blessings to their blessings, and I shall follow that with My blessings and My mercy upon you and upon them. >
> He said that the people then turned to what had been sent down to Moses. Among them will be twelve guardians. Through Muhammad and the message and wisdom with which I send him, I shall complete My religion and seal My prophets and messengers with him. The Hour will come upon Muhammad and his community."

The provenance of that vision is weak. Majlisi takes it from Ibn Tawus, who took it from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani's book of the mutual imprecation, a compiler known for long unverifiable sirah material. It belongs to the dossier as a report, not as evidence of what Abraham saw.

Classified exactly, this line is a reading of the Torah made by Muslims, resting in its strongest form, al-Nu'mani's, on the dictation of a named Jewish scholar, not on a chain to an Imam. Genesis itself then names the twelve princes as Ishmael's own sons, born in his lifetime (Genesis 25:13-16), and that is the natural historical reading of the promise. The Imami application reads the twelve forward into the nation that came from him instead. After al-Nu'mani and al-Rawandi it becomes a standing argument, carried by al-Hurr al-Amili through al-Bayadi and by later scholars in dozens of volumes. The Bible promises twelve princes from Ishmael. The Islamic corpus counts twelve Imams from Ishmael's greatest descendant. The numerical link is a reasoned reading of Genesis 17:20, and its classical home in the school is the Ghayba of al-Nu'mani.

## Twelve Imams in their own reports

The count does not depend on the Bible. The Imami hadith corpus transmits it, and the Tablet of Fatimah ﵍ is its widest report. Al-Kulayni records it in al-Kafi.

Jabir copied the tablet, and Imam al-Baqir ﵇ read the copy back letter for letter. Its text names the twelve in order, from Ali ﵇ the trustee through al-Hasan ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ to "Mim Ha Mim Dal, a mercy to the worlds," the awaited one. Al-Saduq carries the Tablet in Kamal al-Din and Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, al-Tusi in his Ghayba and his Amali, and al-Khazzaz in al-Kifaya, through chains that differ and converge on Jabir.

Beside the Tablet, the count is stated in plain words and preserved in five cited works, Kamal al-Din, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, Ithbat al-Hudat, and Bihar al-Anwar among them.

Kamal al-Din, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, Ithbat al-Hudat, and Bihar al-Anwar all carry it, and al-Hurr al-Amili notes that al-Khazzaz carried it from Ibn Babawayh with the same chain.

The Tradition also ties its twelve to Israel's twelve, in a report whose Sunni chains al-Saduq deliberately records.

Saduq's opening report ties the count to the nuqaba, the twelve tribal chiefs Moses appointed, one from each tribe, when the land was first scouted. The opponents' own widespread reports validate the Imami reports about the twelve Imams, as al-Saduq argues, and al-Kafi carries the comparison with the twelve trustees of Isa ﵇.

The last of the twelve is "a man from the descendants of al-Hasan, who is neither given a kunyah nor named until his affair appears, and he will fill it with justice as it has been filled with tyranny." A kunyah is an honorific byname, Abu so-and-so, and the report's point is that the twelfth one is publicly no one at all until he rises.

## Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon

The Sunni collections carry the number with chains their own scholars grade highly. Sahih Muslim transmits the report of Jabir ibn Samura through a cluster of chains.

> [!note]- The Prophet, Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Imara, Jabir ibn Samura's reports

One clause of this report, "and whose father's name corresponds to my father's name," is absent from Ibn Hanbal's transmissions of the same report, and al-Kanji al-Shafi'i, who collected the Mahdi reports in the seventh century, noted the absence, recorded the harmonizations proposed to keep the clause, and dismissed them as forced. The clause is the one obstacle to reading the report of the twelfth Imam, whose father was al-Hasan ﵇ and not Abdullah, and it is precisely the clause the strongest chains do not carry.

This conflicts with the report of twelve caliphs, for within thirty years there were only the four Rightly Guided Caliphs and the months during which Hasan ibn Ali received allegiance.

Al-Nawawi records the two objections, the thirty-year caliphate report and the plain fact that more than twelve have ruled, and gives al-Qadi Iyad's answers, that the thirty years are the caliphate of prophethood while the twelve carry no such condition, and that the Prophet said twelve would rule, not that only twelve would rule, so the count was already completed and the later rulers do not harm it. The second answer turns the prophecy into a tally of rulers already past. One Sunni voice in Kanz al-Ummal read the whole set as past history, twelve commanders then the Hour, and was corrected by Ibn Abbas himself, as the entry records, that after the twelve come al-Mansur, al-Saffah, and the Mahdi who hands the affair to Isa ﵇.

> "Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence."

Jesus ﵇ before Pilate declines an earthly kingdom. The nations did not stream to Zion's law, the swords did not become plowshares, the dispersed were not gathered under one Davidic shepherd, and Rome was not broken and replaced. The standard Christian answer is that the promises await the second coming, and that answer confirms the essential point. They were not fulfilled by the first advent.

These texts do not logically eliminate the Christian claim that Jesus ﵇ himself returns and performs them. What they eliminate is the claim that they were already fulfilled in the ministry of Jesus of Nazareth. Once the Christian places the fulfillment in the future, the dispute changes its shape. It is no longer whether the prophecies await a future just ruler. It is who that ruler is, and whether the returning Isa ﵇ is himself the king or stands behind another.

| Passage | What it promises | Why the first advent did not exhaust it |
|---|---|---|
| Isaiah 2:2-4, Micah 4:1-4 | Nations judged by God's law, weapons turned to farm tools, war unlearned | No such public order followed in Palestine or in the Christian centuries |
| Isaiah 11:1-9 | A Jesse-rooted ruler judges the poor, slays the wicked, fills the earth with the knowledge of God | The global transformation did not occur |
| Jeremiah 23:5-8, 33:14-16 | A righteous Branch reigns, Judah and Israel dwell securely | No restored, secure Judah and Israel under his rule |
| Ezekiel 37:21-28 | One kingdom, one Davidic shepherd, a permanent sanctuary in the midst | Neither the reunification nor the settled sanctuary occurred |
| Hosea 3:5 | Israel returns and seeks the Lord and David their king in the latter days | The text itself dates the return to the latter days |
| Psalm 72 | The king judges the poor, crushes the oppressor, rules to the ends of the earth, peace while the moon endures | The language is worldwide and governmental and was not realized |
| Daniel 2:44, 7:13-14, 7:27 | God's kingdom crushes and replaces the world kingdoms, all nations serve it | Rome was not crushed or replaced by the mission |

> الحسن ، عن العلاء بن بشير (1) ، عن أبي الصديق الناجي ، عن أبي سعيد الخدري ، عن النبيّ ﵌ أنّه قال : أبشروا بالمهدي ، رجل من عترتي ، يخرج في اختلاف من الناس وزلازل ، فيملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا ، كما ملئت جورا وظلما ، ويرضى عنه ساكن السماء ، وساكن الأرض ، ويقسم المال صحاحا (2) . قالوا : وما صحاحا ؟ قالوا : بالسويّة ، ويملأ اللّه قلوب امّة محمّد ﵌ غناء ، ويسعهم عدله ، حتّى أنّه ليأمر مناديه فينادي : من له إلى مال حاجة ؟ فما يأتيه أحد ، إلّا رجل واحد ، يأتيه فيسأله ، فيقول له : انطلق إلى السادن ، حتّى يعطيك . قال : فيأتيه فيقول له : أنا رسول المهديّ ، لتعطيني مالا ، فيقول له : احث (3) ، فيحثي فلا يستطيع أن يحمله ، فيلقي حتّى يكون قدر ما يستطيع حمله ، فيخرج به ، فيندم . فيقول : إذا ، كنت أجشع امّة محمّد نفسا ، دعتني إلى هذا المال ، وقد تركه غيري ، قال : فيرجع ، فيردّه عليه ، فيقول له : هذا المال لا نقبل منه شيئا ، اعطيناكه . قال : فيلبث بذلك سبعا ، [ أو ] ثمانيا ، [ أو ] تسع سنين (4) ، كذلك لا خير في الحياة بعده (5) .
>
> Al-Hasan, from al-Ala ibn Bashir (1), from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said, "Receive glad tidings of the Mahdi, a man from my progeny. He will emerge amid disagreement among people and earthquakes. He will fill the earth with equity and justice as it has been filled with injustice and oppression. The inhabitant of heaven and the inhabitant of earth will be pleased with him, and he will distribute wealth in full portions (2)."
>
> They said, "What does 'in full portions' mean?" He said, "Equally." God will fill the hearts of Muhammad's community with sufficiency, and his justice will encompass them, so much so that he will order his caller to proclaim, "Who has need of wealth?" No one will come to him except one man. He will come and ask him, and he will say to him, "Go to the keeper, so that he may give you."
>
> He said, "He will go to him and say, 'I am the Mahdi's messenger, so give me wealth.' He will say to him, 'Take a handful' (3). He will take a handful, but will not be able to carry it. So he will put back enough that he can carry, then leave with it and regret it. He will say, 'Then I am the most covetous soul in Muhammad's community. This wealth called me, while others left it.' He will return and give it back to him, but he will say, 'We do not accept anything back from this wealth. We gave it to you.'"
>
> He will remain thus for seven, or eight, or nine years (4). There is no good in life after it (5).

The correspondence with the seventy-second psalm's king is functional. That king judges the poor and the needy, breaks the oppressor, and has dominion from sea to sea. Isaiah's ruler judges the poor with righteousness. The Prophet's ﷺ report makes the Mahdi the one who reverses an earth filled with injustice. The Bible's king brings abundance and peace while the moon endures. The Mahdi's reign fills hearts with sufficiency and empties the treasury of petitioners.

The distinction that matters is the one the reports draw themselves. The returning Isa ﵇ is present, and another is the imam.

> [!note]- Abu Hurayra's report, Musnad Ahmad, vol. 2, p. 336
> (97) حدثنا عبد اللّه ، حدثني أبي ، ثنا عثمان بن عمر ، ثنا ابن أبي ذئب ، عن الزهري ، عن نافع - مولى أبي قتادة - ، عن أبي هريرة : ان النبي ﵆ قال : كيف بكم إذا نزل فيكم عيسى بن مريم وامامكم منكم . 2 / 336
>
> (97) Abdullah narrated to us. My father narrated to me. Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us. Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Nafi', the freedman of Abu Qatada, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet said, "How will you be when Jesus son of Mary descends among you and your imam is from among you?"
>
> Volume 2, page 336.

The report does not name the imam. The Shia corpus names him, in reports that fuse the count, the lineage, and the prayer behind him.

> [!note]- Ibn Abbas's report, Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 51, p. 73, from Kamal al-Din
> 12 - إكمال الدين : ابن مسرور ، عن ابن عامر ، عن المعلى ، عن جعفر بن سليمان ، عن عبد الله بن الحكم ، عن أبيه ، عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله ﵌ : إن خلفائي وأوصيائي وحجج الله على الخلق بعدي اثنا عشر أولهم أخي وآخرهم ولدي وقيل : يا رسول الله ﵌ ومن أخوك ؟ قال : علي بن أبي طالب قيل فمن ولدك ؟ قال : المهدي يملاها قسطا وعدلا كما ملئت جورا وظلما والذي بعثني بالحق نبيا لو لم يبق من الدنيا إلا يوم واحد لأطال الله ذلك اليوم حتى يخرج فيه ولدي المهدي فينزل روح الله عيسى بن مريم ﵇ فيصلي خلفه وتشرق الأرض بنور ربها ويبلغ سلطانه المشرق والمغرب .
>
> Kamal al-Din. Ibn Masrur, from Ibn Amir, from al-Mualla, from Jafar ibn Sulayman, from Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said, "The Messenger of Allah said, 'My successors, my trustees, and Allah's proofs over creation after me are twelve. The first of them is my brother and the last of them is my son.'"
>
> It was said, "Messenger of Allah, who is your brother?" He said, "Ali ibn Abi Talib." It was said, "Then who is your son?" He said, "The Mahdi. He will fill it with equity and justice as it has been filled with tyranny and oppression. By Him who sent me with the truth as a prophet, if only one day remained of the world, Allah would lengthen that day until my son, the Mahdi, emerges in it. Then Jesus son of Mary, the Spirit of Allah, will descend and pray behind him. The earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and his authority will reach the east and the west."

Twelve successors, the first Ali ﵇, the last the Mahdi, and then Isa ﵇ son of Mary, the Spirit of God, descends and prays behind him, and the earth shines with the light of its Lord, and his authority reaches east and west. Imam al-Rida ﵇ states it in al-Ma'mun's own assembly.

> [!info]- Imam al-Rida, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, vol. 2, p. 218
> الرجعة فقال الرضا ﵇ : إنها لحق قد كانت في الأمم السالفة ونطق به القرآن وقد قال رسول الله (ص) يكون في هذه الأمة كل ما كان في الأمم السالفة حذو النعل بالنعل والقذة بالقذة (1) قال ﵇ : إذا خرج المهدي من ولدي نزل عيسى بن مريم ﵇ فصلى خلفه وقال ﵇ : إن الاسلام بدأ غريبا وسيعود غريبا فطوبى للغرباء قيل : يا رسول الله ثم يكون ماذا ؟ قال ثم يرجع الحق إلى أهله فقال المأمون يا أبا الحسن فما تقول في القائلين بالتناسخ ؟ فقال الرضا ﵇ : من قال بالتناسخ فهو كافر بالله العظيم مكذب بالجنة والنار قال المأمون : ما تقول في المسوخ ؟ قال الرضا ﵇ : أولئك قوم غضب الله عليهم فمسخهم فعاشوا ثلاثة أيام ثم ماتوا ولم يتناسلوا فما يوجد في الدنيا من القردة والخنازير وغير ذلك مما وقع عليهم أسم المسوخية فهو مثل ما لا يحل أكلها والانتفاع بها قال المأمون : لا أبقاني الله بعدك يا أبا الحسن فوالله ما يوجد العلم الصحيح إلا عند أهل البيت وإليك انتهت علوم آبائك فجزاك الله عن الاسلام وأهله خيرا قال الحسن بن جهم : فلما قام الرضا ﵇ تبعته فانصرف إلى منزله فدخلت عليه وقلت له : يا بن رسول الله الحمد لله الذي وهب من جميل رأي أمير المؤمنين ﵇ ما حمله ما أرى من إكرامه لك وقبوله لقولك
>
> [He asked about] the return, and al-Rida said, “It is true. It occurred among the former communities, the Quran has spoken of it, and the Messenger of God said, ‘Everything that occurred among the former communities will occur in this community, exactly as one shoe matches the other and one arrow feather matches the other.’”
>
> He said, “When the Mahdi from among my descendants emerges, Jesus son of Mary will descend and pray behind him.”
>
> He said, “Islam began as something strange, and it will return as something strange. Blessed are the strangers.”
>
> It was said, “Messenger of God, then what will happen?” He said, “Then the truth will return to those entitled to it.”
>
> Al-Ma'mun said, “Abu al-Hasan, what do you say about those who hold to transmigration?”
>
> Al-Rida said, “Whoever holds to transmigration disbelieves in God the Almighty and denies Paradise and the Fire.”
>
> Al-Ma'mun said, “What do you say about those who were transformed?”
>
> Al-Rida said, “They were people with whom God was angry, so He transformed them. They lived for three days, then died, and did not reproduce. Thus, the monkeys, pigs, and other creatures found in the world that bear the name of those transformed are like things whose eating and use are not permitted.”
>
> Al-Ma'mun said, “May God not keep me alive after you, Abu al-Hasan. By God, sound knowledge is found only with the People of the House, and the knowledge of your forefathers has come to you. May God reward you well on behalf of Islam and its people.”
>
> Al-Hasan ibn Jahm said, “When al-Rida rose, I followed him. He returned to his house, and I entered upon him and said, ‘Son of the Messenger of God, praise be to God, who granted the Commander of the Faithful such sound judgment as led him to what I see of his honoring you and accepting your words.’”

Al-Kafi carries it in Gabriel's words to the Prophet ﷺ.

> [!info]- Gabriel's words to the Prophet, al-Kafi, vol. 8, p. 74, hadith 10
> الوصيين والحسن والحسين سبطاك سيد الأسباط وحمزة عمك سيد الشهداء وجعفر ابن عمك الطيار في الجنة يطير مع الملائكة حيث يشاء ومنكم القائم يصلي عيسى بن مريم خلفه إذا أهبطه الله إلى الأرض من ذرية علي وفاطمة من ولد الحسين (﵈) .
>
> the trustees, and Hasan and Husayn, your two grandsons, the masters of the grandsons. Hamza, your uncle, is the master of the martyrs. Jafar, your cousin, is the one who flies in Paradise with the angels wherever he wishes. From among you is the Qa'im, behind whom Isa ibn Maryam will pray when God sends him down to the earth. He is from the descendants of Ali and Fatima, from the line of al-Husayn.

> [!info]- Imam al-Hasan, Ithbat al-Hudat, vol. 5, p. 81, report 118
> 118 - وقال : حدثنا المظفر بن جعفر العلوي عن جعفر بن محمّد بن مسعود عن أبيه عن جبرئيل بن أحمد عن موسى بن جعفر البغدادي عن الحسن بن محمّد الصيرفي عن حنان بن سدير عن أبيه عن أبي سعيد عقيصا عن الحسن بن علي ﵇ في حديث قال : أما علمتم أنه ما منا أحد إلا وتقع في عنقه بيعة لطاغية زمانه إلا القائم الذي يصلّي عيسى بن مريم خلفه ، وإن اللّه ﷿ يخفي ولادته ويغيب شخصه لئلا يكون لأحد في عنقه بيعة إذا خرج ذلك التاسع من ولد أخي الحسين ابن سيدة النساء يطيل اللّه عمره في غيبته ثم يظهره بقدرته في صورة شاب ابن دون أربعين سنة ليعلم أن اللّه على كل شيء قدير (4) .
>
> He said, "Al-Muzaffar ibn Jafar al-Alawi narrated to us, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masud, from his father, from Jibril ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Jafar al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, from Hannan ibn Sudayr, from his father, from Abu Said Uqaysa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, in a report in which he said, 'Do you not know that there is none of us except that allegiance to the tyrant of his time falls upon his neck, except the Qa'im, behind whom Jesus son of Mary will pray? Allah conceals his birth and hides his person so that no one's allegiance may be upon his neck when he emerges. That ninth one from the descendants of my brother al-Husayn, son of the Lady of Women, Allah will prolong his life during his occultation, then He will manifest him by His power in the form of a young man under forty years old, so that it may be known that Allah has power over all things.'"

Every one of us bears allegiance to the tyrant of his age on his neck, except the Qa'im, behind whom Isa ﵇ son of Mary will pray. God hides his birth and conceals his person so that no allegiance binds him when he rises.

The Davidic lineage of these kings needs its own word, because the Prophet's ﷺ house is not David's line. The framework already distinguishes the returning Isa ﵇, the son of David, who confirms the truth, from the divinely guided ruler of the final order, and it places the Davidic king inside the Mahdi's kingdom rather than on its throne. A Christian who insists the Davidic king must himself reign has the reports of both traditions to weigh, which give the throne to a man from the Prophet's ﷺ house while Isa ﵇ stands behind him in prayer. The Bible's king who reigns, judges, fights, and fills the earth with justice needs a reign, a judgment, a war, and a transformation. The Gospels record that Isa קּ declined the kingdom before Pilate.

## What the case establishes and what it does not

- **Source:** Christian holders. Pius XII, Munificentissimus Deus 27 (1950) for the Marian reading; Catholic Encyclopedia, "Apocalypse" (1907) for the Church and Israel readings and the Genesis 37 background; Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, p. 130, for the church reading known to Muslim polemic
- **Source:** Islamic exhibits quoted above, Shia and Sunni, cited in their sections
- **Claim:** the compared offices, woman, twelve, and reigning king, and who fills them

Three readings now stand side by side. The Christian readings assign the woman to Mary, to the Church, or to Israel, and assign the reigning king to a future advent of Jesus ﵇. The reading documented above assigns the woman's sun, moon, and twelve stars to the figures the Islamic corpus itself names, the twelve princes of Ishmael to the twelve Imams ﵈, and the reigning king to the Mahdi with Isa ﵇ behind him.

On textual fidelity, the comparison runs this way. The Islamic corpus transmits each element, the sun as the Prophet ﷺ and the moon as Ali ﵇ in the exegesis of Qur'an 91, the nine shining stars as the Imams from al-Husayn's line in the Salman report, the count of twelve in the Tablet and its family of reports, and the justice-filling ruler from Fatimah's ﵍ line. The connection of those fixed elements to the Bible's sign is a modern inference, and each step above has been labeled where inference begins. The Christian readings of the same sign are also assignments, older and internally divided, resting on the authority the reader grants the church. Neither side can prove its assignment from the text alone, because the text names no one.

What the case establishes is narrower and firmer. If the promised Messiah has already come and completed his messianic work, where are the outcomes the prophets promised, the universal law, the peace among nations, the destroyed oppressor kingdoms, the gathered and secure Israel, the worldwide justice? A Christian must answer that they remain future. The question left standing is who fills those offices. The Sunni strand of the reports leaves him unnamed at the descent, and the Imami strand names his line from the children of Fatimah. The Islamic corpus is the one that names him.


## Final Verdict

> [!summary] Final Verdict
> The woman of Revelation 12 is a sign of a sun, a moon, and twelve stars around one woman. The Qur'an swears by the sun and the moon, and the Imams named them the Prophet ﷺ and Ali ﵇. Both schools count twelve from Quraysh, and the Imami reports name all twelve, first Ali קּ and last the Mahdi, eleven of them Fatimah's כֿ descendants. Genesis promises twelve princes from Ishmael, and the line of Ishmael's greatest descendant carried exactly that number of guides. The prophets promise a reigning king of worldwide justice, and the reports of both traditions describe him from the Prophet's ﷺ progeny, with Isa ﵇ returned and praying behind him. The Bible supplies the job description. The Islamic corpus supplies the names. The connection between them is a reading, and each step has been marked where inference begins.

blocks.text: The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars

The Bible's later books describe, without naming anyone, a woman whose sign is a sun, a moon, and a crown of twelve stars (Revelation 12:1), twelve princes from Ishmael (Genesis 17:20), and a future king who judges the poor and fills the earth with justice and the knowledge of God (Isaiah 11:1-9, Psalm 72, Daniel 7:13-14). The Qur'an swears by a sun and by a moon that follows it (Qur'an 91:1-2), and the Imams' transmitted tafsir names that sun as the Prophet ﷺ and that moon as Ali ﵇. Shia and Sunni collections report twelve successors from Quraysh, the Musnad of Ahmad ties the number to the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel, and the Imami reports name twelve Imams, first Ali קּ and last the Mahdi, eleven of them Fatimah's כֿ descendants. Both traditions report an end-time ruler from the Prophet's ﷺ progeny, and reports of both place the returning Isa קּ beside him rather than on his throne. The conclusion is a weighed reading. The Bible's unnamed figures and the Islamic corpus's named figures carry the same assignments, so the Bible carries the job description and the Islamic reports carry the names of those who fill it.

blocks.text: No verse names the house

No verse of the Hebrew Bible or the New Testament names Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, or any Imam. Christians who expect a coming king read the same books and find Jesus ﵇ in them. A claim that the Bible contains the Prophet's family by name would be false, and the case made here does not rest on one.

What the Bible does contain is a set of unnamed figures defined by relations and by work. A woman stands clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet and a crown of twelve stars (Revelation 12:1). Ishmael is promised twelve princes and a great nation (Genesis 17:20). A future king from Jesse judges the poor with righteousness, kills the wicked, and fills the earth with the knowledge of God (Isaiah 11:1-9). The question here is narrow. Do the job descriptions the Bible assigns to its unnamed figures match the assignments the Islamic corpus itself makes, in its own reports, to the Prophet's house?

That question can be answered without forcing a single verse. The Qur'an swears by a sun and a moon, and the Imams' transmitted exegesis names that sun and that moon. The Prophet ﷺ is reported in Shia and Sunni collections alike to have counted twelve successors and to have tied that number to the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel. He is reported to have described an end-time ruler from Fatimah's ﵍ descendants who fills the earth with justice, and to have distinguished that ruler from the returning Isa ﵇. If those reports carry the Tradition's own assignment of the sky's lights to the Prophet's house, and its own count of twelve, then the Bible's woman, its twelve princes, and its reigning king describe a configuration the Islamic sources had already assembled under names.
A match of assignments is a reading, and a reading can be weighed. It is not a named prophecy, and it does not refute a Christian who assigns the same texts to a future advent of Jesus ﵇.
