Revelation 12:17, Textus Receptus, Van Dyck, King James Version και ωργισθη ο δρακων επι τη γυναικι και απηλθεν ποιησαι πολεμον μετα των λοιπων του σπερματος αυτης των τηρουντων τας εντολας του θεου και εχοντων την μαρτυριαν του ιησου χριστου 17 فغضب التنين على المرأة وذهب ليصنع حربا مع باقي نسلها الذين يحفظون وصايا الله وعندهم شهادة يسوع المسيح kai ōrgisthē ho drakōn epi tē gunaiki, kai apēlthen poiēsai polemon meta tōn loipōn tou spermatos autēs, tōn tērountōn tas entolas tou theou kai echontōn tēn marturian Iēsou christou. "And the dragon was wroth with the woman, and went to make war with the remnant of her seed, which keep the commandments of God, and have the testimony of Jesus Christ."

Three elements define the woman. She is associated with the sun, with the moon, and with exactly twelve stars. The dragon is identified within the chapter itself as Satan (Revelation 12:9), and the male child is the one destined to rule the nations. The passage does not name the woman, and readers have supplied the name for two thousand years.
Who the churches say she is

Christian interpretation has never settled on one woman. Pope Pius XII, defining the Assumption of Mary in 1950, wrote that the scholastic doctors recognized the Assumption as signified in "that woman clothed with the sun whom John the Apostle contemplated on the Island of Patmos" (Munificentissimus Deus 27). The Catholic Encyclopedia's article on the Apocalypse states the historical-critical reading in one line. "The woman in travail is a personification of the synagogue or the church. Her first-born is Christ, her other seed is the community of the faithful" (Van den Biesen, "Apocalypse," 1907). The same article reads the imagery through Israel's own scriptures, noting the crown of twelve stars and the sun and moon under her feet with a cross-reference to Genesis 37:9-10, Joseph's dream.

The standard Christian identifications are Mary, the Church, and Israel, and the encyclopedia's own cross-reference sends the image back to Joseph's dream, in which the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 37:9). On the Israel reading the woman is Jacob's household and the sign retells the dream. That explains where the image came from. It does not settle who the woman is, and the chapter's war between her seed and the dragon still asks for her. None of these readings is a fact about the text. Each is an assignment, and the assignment has to fit the figure's relations. A woman whose sign is a sun she wears, a moon under her feet, and twelve stars as her crown is a woman set among those lights, and any reading of her names a household for them.
An oath by the sun and the moon
The Qur'an opens the ninety-first sura with an oath.

Qur'an 91:1-4, as cited in Ta'wil al-Ayat, vol. 2, p. 367 قال الله تعالى : بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والشمس وضحاها (1) والقمر إذا تلاها (2) والنهار إذا جلاها (3) والليل إذا يغشاها (4) Bismi llahi r-rahmani r-rahim. Wa-sh-shamsi wa-duhaha, wa-l-qamari idha talaha, wa-n-nahari idha jallaha, wa-l-layli idha yaghshaha. God, Most High, said, "In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. By the sun and its morning brightness (1), and by the moon when it follows it (2), and by the day when it reveals it (3), and by the night when it covers it (4)."
The verb of the oath is tala, to follow. Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi records the reading of the school with a full chain.

Imam al-Sadiq, Tafsir al-Qummi, vol. 2, p. 424 سورة الشمس مكية آياتها خمس عشرة (بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم والشمس وضحاها) قال : أخبرني أبي عن سليمان الديلمي عن أبي بصير عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : سألته عن قول الله ﷿ والشمس وضحاها ، قال : الشمس رسول الله ﵌ أوضح الله به للناس دينهم قلت : (والقمر إذا تلاها) قال ذلك أمير المؤمنين (ع) قلت : (والليل إذا يغشاها) قال : ذلك أئمة الجور الذين استبدوا للامر دون آل رسول الله ﵌ وجلسوا مجلسا كان آل رسول الله ﵌ أولى به منهم ، فغشوا دين رسول الله ﵌ بالظلم والجور وهو قوله : والليل إذا يغشاها ، قال : يغشى ظلمهم ضوء النهار ، قلت : (والنهار إذا جلاها) قال : ذلك الامام من ذرية فاطمة ﵍ يسئل عن دين رسول الله فيجلى لمن يسأله ، Surat al-Shams is Meccan. Its verses are fifteen. In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. "By the sun and its morning brightness." He said, "My father informed me from Sulayman al-Daylami, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, 'I asked him about the saying of God, "By the sun and its morning brightness." He said, "The sun is the Messenger of God. Through him God made His religion clear to the people." I said, "And the moon when it follows it." He said, "That is the Commander of the Faithful." I said, "And the night when it covers it." He said, "Those are the imams of tyranny who seized authority apart from the family of the Messenger of God and occupied a position to which the family of the Messenger of God had a greater right than they did. They covered the religion of the Messenger of God with wrongdoing and tyranny. This is His saying, 'And the night when it covers it.' Their wrongdoing covers the light of day." I said, "And the day when it makes it clear." He said, "That is the imam from the descendants of Fatimah. He is asked about the religion of the Messenger of God, and he makes it clear for whoever asks him.'"

The sun is Muhammad ﷺ, through whom God made the religion clear. The moon that follows him is Ali ﵇. The night that covers is the seizure of rule from the family of the Messenger ﷺ. The day that reveals is an Imam from Fatimah's ﵍ descendants who answers questions about the Prophet's religion. Furat ibn Ibrahim al-Kufi, who died in the fourth century, carries the same distribution from al-Husayn ﵇ himself.

Al-Husayn, Tafsir Furat al-Kufi, p. 563, report 721 721 - 3 فرات قال : حدثني علي بن محمد بن عمر الزهري معنعنا : عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال : قال الحارث [بن عبد الله] الأعور للحسين ﵇ : يا ابن رسول الله جعلت فداك أخبرني عن قول الله في كتابه : (والشمس وضحاها) قال : ويحك يا حارث ذلك محمد رسول الله ﵌ . قال : قلت : جعلت فداك : قوله : (والقمر إذا تلاها) قال : ذلك أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ يتلو محمدا ﵌ . قال : قلت : (والنهار إذا جلاها) قال : ذلك القائم من آل محمد ﵌ يملأ الأرض عدلا وقسطا . Furat said, "Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Umar al-Zuhri narrated to me, with a chain of transmission, from Abu Jafar, who said, 'Al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-Awar said to al-Husayn, "O son of the Messenger of Allah, may I be made your ransom, tell me about God's saying in His Book, 'By the sun and its brightness.'" He said, "Woe to you, Harith. That is Muhammad, the Messenger of God." He said, "I said, 'May I be made your ransom. His saying, 'And by the moon when it follows it.'" He said, "That is the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib, following Muhammad." He said, "I said, 'And by the day when it reveals it.'" He said, "That is the Qa'im from the family of Muhammad. He will fill the earth with justice and equity."'"

The answer to the opening question is yes. In the Imami transmission the sun of the oath is the Prophet ﷺ and its moon is Ali ﵇, and the day is the Qa'im, the one who rises, who fills the earth with justice. The reading is not a single stray voice. Al-Kulayni's al-Kafi carries it in the Rawda volume, and al-Qummi and Furat carry it through independent chains, with Ibn Abbas versions beside them in Furat and Ibn Shahrashub. One recorded variant assigns the figures differently.

Imam al-Sadiq, Ta'wil al-Ayat, vol. 2, pp. 367-368, minority channel لهذه تأويل ظاهر وباطن : فالظاهر ظاهر ، وأما الباطن فهو : 1 - ما رواه علي بن محمد ، عن أبي جميلة ، عن الحلبي . ورواه (أيضا) (1) علي بن الحكم ، عن أبان بن عثمان ، عن الفضل بن العباس عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ (أنه) (2) قال (والشمس وضحاها) الشمس : أمير المؤمنين ﵇ " وضحاها " قيام القائم (3) ﵇ (لان الله سبحانه قال (وأن يحشر الناس ضحى) (4) . (والقمر إذا تلاها) الحسن والحسين ﵉ . (والنهار إذا جلاها) هو قيام القائم ﵇ . (والليل إذا يغشاها) حبتر (ودولته قد غشى) (5) عليه الحق . وأما قوله (والسماء وما بناها) قال : هو محمد - عليه وآله السلام - هو السماء الذي يسموا إليه الخلف في العلم . This has an outward interpretation and an inward interpretation. The outward is outward. As for the inward interpretation, it is as follows. Ali ibn Muhammad narrated from Abu Jamilah, from al-Halabi. Ali ibn al-Hakam also narrated it from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas, from Abu Abd Allah, who said, "By the sun and its morning brightness. The sun is the Commander of the Faithful. Its morning brightness is the rising of the Qa'im, because God, exalted is He, said, 'And that the people will be gathered in the morning.' And the moon when it follows it refers to Hasan and Husayn." "And the day when it reveals it" is the rising of the Qa'im. "And the night when it covers it" is Habtar, and his rule has covered the truth. As for His saying, "And the heaven and He who built it," he said, "It is Muhammad. He is the heaven to which successors ascend in knowledge."

In this version the sun is Ali ﵇, the moon is al-Hasan and al-Husayn ﵈, and the heaven is Muhammad ﷺ. Sharaf al-Din al-Astarabadi, who collected it in Ta'wil al-Ayat, transmits it through two chains that converge on one report, the line of Abu Jamila from al-Halabi beside the line of Ali ibn al-Hakam, and al-Burhan and Bihar al-Anwar carry it from him rather than independently. The version that makes the sun the Prophet ﷺ and the moon Ali ﵇ is the one with the wider distribution in the early collections, in al-Kafi, al-Qummi, Furat, and Ibn Shahrashub's Manaqib. In the early transmission of the school, that is the reading of the oath the woman of Revelation 12 would need.
The lights of one house
The reports do not leave the sun and the moon as a pair. Al-Saduq devotes a chapter of Ma'ani al-Akhbar to the question and gathers three chains to one report.

The Prophet, Ma'ani al-Akhbar, pp. 208-209, with three chains, p. 208 (باب) (معنى الشمس والقمر والزهرة والفرقدين) 1 - حدثنا أبو الحسن محمد بن عمر [و] بن علي بن عبد الله البصري ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر عبد الله بن علي الكرخي ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر محمد بن عبد الله ، قال : حدثنا أبي قال : حدثنا عبد الرزاق الصنعاني ، قال : حدثنا معمر ، عن الزهري ، عن أنس بن مالك قال : صلى رسول الله ﵌ صلاة الفجر ، فلما انفتل من صلاته أقبل علينا بوجهه الكريم على الله ﷿ ثم قال : معاشر الناس من افتقد الشمس فليستمسك بالقمر ، ومن افتقد القمر فليستمسك بالزهرة ، فمن افتقد الزهرة فليستمسك (2) بالفرقدين . ثم قال رسول الله ﵌ : أنا الشمس ، وعلي القمر ، وفاطمة الزهرة ، والحسن والحسين الفرقدان . وكتاب الله لا يفترقان حتى يردا علي الحوض . - 2 حدثنا أبو الحسن محمد بن عمر [و] البصري ، قال : حدثنا أبو القاسم نصر بن الحسين الصفار النهاوندي بها ، قال : حدثنا أبو الفرج أحمد بن محمد بن خوزي السامري ، قال : حدثنا أبو بكر القاسم بن إبراهيم القنطري ، قال : حدثنا إبراهيم بن خالد الحلواني ، قال حدثنا محمد بن خلف العسقلاني ، قال : حدثنا محمد بن السري ، عن محمد بن المنكدر ، عن جابر بن عبد الله ، قال . قال رسول الله ﵌ : اقتدوا بالشمس فإذا غابت الشمس فاقتدوا Chapter on the meaning of the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqads Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abd Allah al-Basri narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr Abd Allah ibn Ali al-Karkhi narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah narrated to us. He said that his father narrated to us. He said that Abd al-Razzaq al-San'ani narrated to us from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, who said The Messenger of God performed the dawn prayer. When he had turned away after his prayer, he turned toward us with his noble face, God exalted be He, and said, "People, whoever loses the sun should hold fast to the moon. Whoever loses the moon should hold fast to Venus. Whoever loses Venus should hold fast to the two Farqads." Then the Messenger of God said, "I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Fatima is Venus, and Hasan and Husayn are the two Farqads. They and the Book of God will not separate until they come to me at the Pool." Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Umar al-Basri narrated to us. He said that Abu al-Qasim Nasr ibn al-Husayn al-Saffar al-Nahawandi narrated to us there. He said that Abu al-Faraj Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khuwayzi al-Samiri narrated to us. He said that Abu Bakr al-Qasim ibn Ibrahim al-Qantari narrated to us. He said that Ibrahim ibn Khalid al-Hulwani narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn al-Sari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said The Messenger of God said, "Follow the sun. When the sun sets, follow"

The Prophet, Ma'ani al-Akhbar, pp. 208-209, with three chains, continued, p. 209 بالقمر ، فإذا غاب القمر فاقتدوا بالزهرة فإذا غابت الزهرة فاقتدوا بالفرقدين فقالوا : يا رسول الله فما الشمس ؟ وما القمر ؟ وما الزهرة ؟ وما الفرقدان ؟ فقال : أنا الشمس ، وعلي القمر ، والزهرة فاطمة ، والفرقدان الحسن والحسين by the moon. When the moon disappears, follow Venus. When Venus disappears, follow the two Farqad stars." They said, "Messenger of God, what are the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqad stars?" He said, "I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Venus is Fatimah, and the two Farqad stars are Hasan and Husayn."

The five lights of the sky are the five of the house, and the report is not Shia property alone. Al-Safuri al-Shafi'i carries it in Nuzhat al-Majalis and names his source, al-Thalabi's Ara'is, and al-Natanzi carries it in al-Khasais.

The Prophet, Nuzhat al-Majalis, vol. 2, p. 315, citing al-Thalabi's Ara'is وفي حديث آخر : «من افتقد الشمس فليتمسك بالقمر ومن افتقد القمر فليتمسك بالزهرة ومن افتقد الزهرة فليتمسك بالفرقدين فسئل عن ذلك فقال : أنا الشمس وعلي القمر والزهرة فاطمة والفرقدان الحسن والحسين ﵃» ذكره في العرائس In another report, "Whoever loses the sun should hold fast to the moon. Whoever loses the moon should hold fast to Venus. Whoever loses Venus should hold fast to the two Farqads." He was asked about this and said, "I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Venus is Fatimah, and the two Farqads are Hasan and Husayn." He mentioned it in al-Ara'is.
Al-Khazzaz al-Qummi extends the constellation to the full twelve, in the report of Salman.

The Prophet, Kifayat al-Athar, pp. 65-66, Salman's report, p. 65 معاشر الناس من افتقد الشمس فليتمسك بالقمر ، ومن افتقد القمر فليتمسك بالفرقدين ، فإذا فقدتم الفرقدين فتمسكوا بالنجوم الزاهرة بعدي ، أقول قولي هذا وأستغفر الله لي ولكم . قال : فلما نزل عن المنبر ﵌ تبعته حتى دخل بيت عائشة ، فدخلت إليه وقلت : بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله سمعتك تقول " إذا افتقدتم الشمس فتمسكوا بالقمر ، وإذا افتقدتم القمر فتمسكوا بالفرقدين ، وإذا افتقدتم الفرقدين فتمسكوا بالنجوم الزاهرة " فما الشمس وما القمر وما الفرقدان وما النجوم الزاهرة ؟ فقال : [أنا الشمس (2) وعلي القمر والحسن والحسين الفرقدان ، فإذا افتقدتموني فتمسكوا بعلي بعدي ، وإذا افتقدتموه فتمسكوا بالحسن والحسين] ، وأما النجوم الزاهرة فهم الأئمة (3) التسعة (4) "People, whoever loses the sun, let him hold fast to the moon. Whoever loses the moon, let him hold fast to the two Farqads. When you lose the two Farqads, hold fast after me to the shining stars. I say these words of mine and ask God to forgive me and you." He said, "When he came down from the pulpit, I followed him until he entered the house of Aisha. I entered upon him and said, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of God. I heard you say, "When you lose the sun, hold fast to the moon. When you lose the moon, hold fast to the two Farqads. When you lose the two Farqads, hold fast to the shining stars." What are the sun, the moon, the two Farqads, and the shining stars?' He said, 'I am the sun, Ali is the moon, and Hasan and Husayn are the two Farqads. When you lose me, hold fast after me to Ali. When you lose him, hold fast to Hasan and Husayn. As for the shining stars, they are the nine Imams'

The Prophet, Kifayat al-Athar, pp. 65-66, Salman's report, continued, p. 66 من صلب الحسين ، تاسعهم (1) مهديهم . ثم قال ﵇ : إنهم هم الأوصياء والخلفاء بعدي ، أئمة أبرار ، عدد أسباط يعقوب وحواري عيسى . قلت : فسمهم لي يا رسول الله ؟ قال : أولهم (2) علي بن أبي طالب ، وبعده (3) سبطاي ، وبعدهما علي (4) زين العابدين ، وبعده محمد بن علي الباقر (5) علم النبيين والصادق (6) جعفر بن محمد وابنه الكاظم سمي موسى بن عمران والذي يقتل بأرض الغربة (7) ابنه (8) علي ثم ابنه محمد (9) والصادقان علي والحسن والحجة القائم المنتظر في غيبته ، from the loins of Husayn, the ninth of whom is their Mahdi." Then he said, "They are the legatees and caliphs after me, righteous Imams, equal in number to the tribes of Yaqub and the apostles of Isa." I said, "Name them for me, O Messenger of God." He said, "The first of them is Ali ibn Abi Talib. After him are my two grandsons. After them are Ali Zayn al-Abidin, then Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, the knowledge of the prophets, al-Sadiq Jafar ibn Muhammad, his son al-Kazim, the namesake of Musa ibn Imran, and the one who will be killed in the land of exile, his son Ali, then his son Muhammad, the two truthful ones Ali and Hasan, and the Proof, the Qa'im awaited during his occultation,"

The shining stars are the nine Imams from al-Husayn's ﵇ loins, the ninth their Mahdi, and the count is tied, in the Prophet's ﷺ own words as reported, to the twelve tribes of Yaqub and the twelve apostles of Isa ﵇. Count the figures. Revelation places a woman, a sun, a moon, and twelve stars in one sign. The code places the sun, the moon, Venus, and the two Farqads over the Prophet ﷺ, Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, al-Hasan ﵇, and al-Husayn ﵇, and the shining stars over the nine Imams after al-Husayn ﵇. No report assigns the crown itself. The reports give the moon to Ali, the two Farqads to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and nine shining stars to the Imams after al-Husayn, while the Tablet family of reports counts the Imams as twelve. Reading Revelation's crown of twelve as those twelve Imams, with Ali among them beside his moon, is where the inference begins.
One qualification belongs here, because the obvious bridge from Joseph's dream to the Imams has no classical support. The Imam-side tafsirs of Qur'an 12:4 read Joseph's dream literally.

Imam al-Baqir, Tafsir al-Qummi, vol. 1, p. 365, Abu al-Jarud's report ثم قص قصة يوسف لأبيه (يا أبت اني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين) حدثنا محمد بن جعفر قال حدثنا محمد بن أحمد قال حدثنا علي بن محمد عمن حدثه عن المنقري عن عمرو بن شمر عن إسماعيل السندي عن عبد الرحمن ابن سابط القرشي عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري في قول الله ﷿ " اني رأيت أحد عشر كوكبا والشمس والقمر رأيتهم لي ساجدين " قال في تسمية النجوم هو الطارق وحوبان والذيال (الدبال ك) وذو الكتفين (ذو الكنفين ط) ووثاب وقابس وعمودان وفليق (فيلق) ومصبح والصرح والفروع (والقروع) والضياء والنور يعني الشمس والقمر وكل هذه النجوم محيطة بالسماء ، وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال تأويل هذه الرؤيا انه سيملك مصر ويدخل عليه أبواه واخوته ، اما الشمس فأم يوسف راحيل والقمر يعقوب واما أحد عشر كوكبا فاخوته ، فلما دخلوا عليه سجدوا شكرا لله وحده حين نظروا إليه وكان ذلك السجود لله . Then he related Joseph's story to his father. "My father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon. I saw them prostrating themselves before me." Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to us. He said that Ali ibn Muhammad narrated to us from one who narrated to him, from al-Minqari, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Isma'il al-Sindi, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit al-Qurashi, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, concerning the saying of God, "I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon. I saw them prostrating themselves before me." He said concerning the names of the stars, "They are al-Tariq, Hawban, al-Dhiyal, al-Dibbal in K, Dhu al-Katifayn, Dhu al-Kanafayn in T, Waththab, Qabis, Amudan, Faliq, Faylaq, Musbih, al-Sarh, al-Furu', al-Quru' in the variant reading, al-Diya', and al-Nur, meaning the sun and the moon. All these stars surround the sky." In the report of Abu al-Jarud from Abu Ja'far, he said, "The interpretation of this vision is that he will rule Egypt, and his parents and brothers will enter upon him. The sun was Joseph's mother Rachel, the moon was Jacob, and the eleven stars were his brothers. When they entered upon him, they prostrated in thanks to God alone when they saw him. That prostration was for God."

The sun is Joseph's mother, the moon is Jacob, and the eleven stars are the brothers. The stars' names are even listed. No classical Imam-side exegesis of 12:4 known to this corpus reads the dream as the Prophet's ﵇ house. The assignments of the sky's lights above stand on their own reports. Reading Revelation 12 through them is an inference of the argument, not a transmitted interpretation.
The Fatimah reading and its history

Labib Baydun, Mawsu'at Karbala, vol. 1, p. 131 45 - الإنجيل يتنبّأ بالأئمة الاثني عشر : جاء في الإصحاح الحادي عشر عن تنبؤات يوحنا اللاهوتي ما نصه : « وظهرت آية عظيمة في السماء ، امرأة متسربلة بالشمس ، وتحت رجليها القمر ، وعلى رأسها إكليل من اثني عشر كوكبا » . فكأنه يتكلم عن مولاتنا فاطمة الزهراء ﵍ وقد تسربلت بالشمس يعني أبيها محمّد ﵌ ، وتزوجت بالقمر وهو علي بن أبي طالب ﵇ ، وعلى رأسها إكليل من أبنائها المعصومين الاثني عشر ، الذين أولهم الحسن والحسين وآخرهم المهدي ﵇ . وليس هناك فيما تنبّأ به يوحنا اللاهوتي فيما سيحصل من أمور ، شيء شبيه بالذي ذكر ، غير فاطمة وأبيها وبعلها وبنيها ﵈ . The Gospel foretells the twelve Imams. In the eleventh chapter, the following occurs among the prophecies of John the Theologian. "A great sign appeared in heaven, a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars." It is as though he is speaking of our lady Fatima al-Zahra. She was clothed with the sun, meaning her father Muhammad, and married to the moon, who is Ali ibn Abi Talib. Upon her head is a crown from her twelve infallible sons, the first of whom are al-Hasan and al-Husayn and the last of whom is the Mahdi. Among what John the Theologian foretold would occur, there is nothing resembling what he mentioned except Fatima, her father, her husband, and her sons.

The mapping is complete, woman, sun, moon, crown, and the encyclopedia's phrase about the sons strains the arithmetic by one, since eleven of the twelve descend from her and the count includes her husband. The full form, with the dragon and the child, appears in the earliest Imami carrier found, Ilzam al-Nasib of al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, written in the early fourteenth century AH. His rendering of the vision paraphrases loosely and folds in clauses about mountains lowered and rough places smoothed that Revelation itself does not carry; the exhibit keeps his text as it stands.

Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, pp. 129-130, p. 129 البشارة السابعة عشرة في قوام الأمة عن مكاشفات يوحنا في الباب الثاني عشر في الآية الأولى ما ترجمته : إنه ظهر في السماء علامة وهي امرأة لبست الشمس ، وتحت رجليها القمر ، وعلى رأسها تاج من اثني عشر كوكبا ، فبينما هي حامل وإذا بثعبان سيمتلئ ، وكل جبل وأكمة ستتضع وتعتدل المعوجات وتلين الصعاب ، تلك الكواكب على الأرض والثعبان واقفة عند المرأة الحاملة على الوضع لتأخذ مولودها بعد وضعها ، فوضعت ذكرا سويا يحكم على جميع الطوائف بعصا من حديد ، فاجتلب وأخذ إلى الله وبلغ إلى مقرره وسريره ، انتهى (2) . قال المؤلف : المراد بالامرأة هي فاطمة الزهراء حيث غلبت نورها الشمس ، والقمر تحت رجلها وهي أعلى وأجل ، بل نوره جزء من آلاف جزء من أجزاء نورها ومكتسب منها ، والتاج المشتمل على البروج الاثني عشر الأئمة الاثنا عشر سلام الله عليهم أجمعين ، والمراد من تلك الثعبان شجرة بني أمية ، الشجرة الخبيثة ، قتلت الكواكب المعنوية المشرقة ، والمراد من الطفل هو الإمام القائم (﵇) الغائب ، حيث أراد الأعداء قتله فاختفى وحجب عن الأبصار ، والعصا الحديد كناية عن السيف ، فيقاتل من على وجه الأرض من الطوائف بالسيف ويملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا ويضمحل وينهدم بنيان الكفر والضلال والظلم ، وليس مراد اليسوع المسيح لأنه (﵇) لم يقاتل قط ، وإنما كان المسيح مظهرا للرحمة ، ويمكن أن يكون المراد من النجوم الاثني عشر محمدا (﵌) وعليا والعشرة من أولاده ، والقمر كناية عن القائم (﵇) ، ولا ينطبق على مريم واليسوع والحواريين ، لأنهم وإن كانوا اثني عشر إلا أنه ارتد واحد منهم فينافي العدد المعلوم . The seventeenth glad tiding concerning the support of the community is from the Revelations of John, in chapter twelve, verse one. Its translation is as follows. "A sign appeared in heaven. It was a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and a crown of twelve stars upon her head. While she was pregnant, behold, a serpent will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be lowered, the crooked places will be made straight, and the rough places will become smooth. Those stars are upon the earth, and the serpent stands before the woman who is pregnant and about to give birth, in order to take her child after she gives birth. So she gave birth to a sound male, who rules all the groups with an iron rod. He was carried away and taken to God, and reached His abode and throne." End. The author said, "What is meant by the woman is Fatimah al-Zahra, for her light surpassed the sun. The moon is beneath her foot, and she is higher and more majestic. Indeed, its light is one part of thousands of parts of portions of her light and is acquired from her. The crown containing the twelve constellations is the twelve Imams, peace be upon them all. What is meant by that serpent is the tree of Banu Umayyah, the wicked tree. It killed the shining spiritual stars. What is meant by the child is the hidden Imam, the Qa'im. Since the enemies wanted to kill him, he concealed himself and was veiled from sight. The iron rod is a metaphor for the sword. He will fight the groups upon the face of the earth with the sword, fill the earth with equity and justice, and the structure of unbelief, error, and oppression will vanish and collapse. Jesus the Messiah is not meant, because he never fought. Rather, the Messiah was a manifestation of mercy. It is possible that the twelve stars mean Muhammad, Ali, and ten of his sons, and that the moon is a metaphor for the Qa'im. It does not apply to Mary, Jesus, and the disciples, because although they were twelve, one of them apostatized, which conflicts with the known number."

Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, pp. 129-130, continued, p. 130 وما فسره بعض علماء النصارى من أن المراد من المرأة هي المعبد والكنيسة ، والنجوم الاثني عشر عبارة عن الحوراء الملازمة لها الحافات حولها ، وذلك حيث ذكر في الباب الثاني من المكاشفات أن اكتب للحوراء الموكلة بكنيسة أقس أن من بيده النجوم السبع يسير في المصابيح السبعة المذهبة ، ففيه أن الكنايس لا تشتمل على الحور ولا يناسب ذكر النجم لها أيضا وبعيد جدا ، والتعبير عن الخادم والحارث والحفظة مع ما هم عليه من الظلمة بالنورانية والبهاء أبعد خطأ عند العقلاء . What some Christian scholars interpreted is that the woman means the temple and the church, and that the twelve stars refer to the maidens attached to her and surrounding her. This is because chapter two of the Apocalypse mentions, "Write to the maiden appointed over the church of Ephesus, that He who holds the seven stars walks among the seven golden lampstands." Yet churches do not contain maidens, nor is it fitting to call her a star. This is very far-fetched. Moreover, to describe the servant, the cultivator, and the guards, despite their darkness, as luminous and radiant is an even more erroneous mistake in the judgment of rational people.

Al-Ha'iri reads the dragon as the tree of Banu Umayyah, the male child as the hidden Qa'im, and the iron rod as his sword, and he argues that the child cannot be Jesus ﵇ because Jesus ﵇ never fought. He records the Christian exegesis of his own day, which read the woman as the temple or the church, and rejects it, and he offers an alternative distribution of his own in which the twelve stars are Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇, and ten of his descendants and the moon is the Qa'im.

The provenance has a limit that matters. A corpus search for the woman of Revelation 12 across the classical Imami literature, al-Kafi, the tafsirs, Bihar al-Anwar in its hundred and more volumes, returns nothing before the modern period. The earliest explicit carrier found is Ilzam al-Nasib. The argumentative ancestry runs through Jawad ibn Ibrahim Sabat al-Hanafi, whose Revelation material later Imami authors recycled, and Milani's Nafahat al-Azhar carries that line in its eighteenth volume. The modern authors also disagree with one another. One makes the sun Ali ﵇ and the woman's travail her miscarriage of Muhsin, and one makes the woman Narjis, the Mahdi's mother, with the sun as Imam al-Hasan al-Askari ﵇. The reading of the woman as Fatimah ﵍, with her father as the sun and her husband as the moon, is the commonest modern form, and Mawsu'at Karbala states it in its cleanest shape. (The encyclopedia's chapter reference slips by one. The quotation is Revelation 12:1.)

The classical Imami corpus never reads Revelation 12, and the reading of it as Fatimah ﵍ is modern. The modern reading assembles elements the classical corpus had already transmitted, the sun as the Prophet ﷺ and the moon as Ali ﵇ in the exegesis of Qur'an 91, the nine shining stars as the Imams from al-Husayn's line in the Salman report, and the woman as the one whose father, husband, and descendants they are. The Bible supplies a sign whose elements are a sun, a moon, and twelve stars around one woman. The Islamic corpus supplies a house whose members carry exactly those signs. The connection between the two is a modern inference, and it stands here as one.
Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael
The numerical promise is older than Revelation.

Genesis 17:20, Westminster Leningrad Codex, Van Dyck, King James Version וּֽלְיִשְׁמָעֵאל֮ שְׁמַעְתִּיךָ֒ הִנֵּ֣ה ׀ בֵּרַ֣כְתִּי אֹתֹ֗ו וְהִפְרֵיתִ֥י אֹתֹ֛ו וְהִרְבֵּיתִ֥י אֹתֹ֖ו בִּמְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נְשִׂיאִם֙ יֹולִ֔יד וּנְתַתִּ֖יו לְגֹ֥וי גָּדֹֽול׃ 20 وأما إسماعيل فقد سمعت لك فيه . هاأنا أباركه وأثمره وأكثره كثيرا جدا . اثني عشر رئيسا يلد وأجعله أمة كبيرة uleyishma'el shema'tikha, hinneh berakhtiv vehifreitiv vehirbeitiv bime'od me'od. sheneim-asar nesi'im yolid, unetativ legoy gadol. "And as for Ishmael, I have heard thee: Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him exceedingly; twelve princes shall he beget, and I will make him a great nation."

The Prophet ﷺ descends from Ishmael in the accepted Islamic genealogy, and the tradition read the blessing with its own count in view. Al-Nu'mani, writing his Book of Occultation in the fourth century, is the earliest explicit carrier of the equation.

Al-Nu'mani, Kitab al-Ghayba, p. 108, from a Jewish scholar of Arrajan وقد أجبت دعاءك في إسماعيل ، وقد سمعتك ما باركته ، وسأكثره جدا جدا ، وسيلد اثني عشر عظيما أجعلهم أئمة كشعب عظيم . أقرأني عبد الحليم بن الحسين السمري (﵀) ما أملاه عليه رجل من اليهود بأرجان (1) يقال له الحسين بن سليمان من علماء اليهود بها من أسماء الأئمة (﵈) بالعبرانية وعدتهم ، وقد أثبته على لفظه ، وكان فيما قرأه أنه يبعث من ولد إسماعيل في التوراة اشموعيل يسمى مابد (2) يعني محمدا (﵌) يكون سيدا ، ويكون من آله اثنا عشر رجلا أئمة وسادة يقتدى بهم ، وأسماؤهم : تقوبيت ، فيذوا ، ذبيرا ، مفسورا ، مسموعا ، دوموه ، ثبو ، هذار ، يثمو ، بطور ، نوقس ، قيدموا . "I have answered your prayer concerning Ishmael. I have heard you and blessed him. I shall multiply him exceedingly, exceedingly. He will father twelve great men, and I shall make them imams for a great people." Abd al-Halim ibn al-Husayn al-Samuri read to me what a Jewish man in Arrajan, called al-Husayn ibn Sulayman, one of its Jewish scholars, dictated to him concerning the names of the imams in Hebrew and their number. I have recorded it in its own wording. Among what he read was that in the Torah, one will be sent from the descendants of Ishmael, called Ashmu'il, and named Mabad, meaning Muhammad. He will be a master, and from his family will be twelve men, imams and masters to be followed. Their names are Taqwabit, Fidhwa, Dhabira, Mafsura, Masmu'a, Dumuha, Thabu, Hadhar, Yathmu, Batur, Nuqus, and Qayduma.

A Jewish scholar of Arrajan dictates, from the Torah in Hebrew, that from Ishmael's line comes a master called Mabad, meaning Muhammad ﷺ, and from his family twelve men, imams and masters, and he lists their twelve names in Hebrew. Al-Rawandi's Kharaij carries the Torah quotation with the gloss attached.

Al-Rawandi, al-Kharaij wa-l-Jara'ih, vol. 1, p. 77 منها ألفاظ التوراة في هذا الباب في السفر الأول منه : " إن الملك نزل على إبراهيم فقال له : إنه يولد في هذا العالم لك غلام اسمه إسحاق . فقال إبراهيم : ليت إسماعيل يعيش بين أيديك بخدمتك . فقال الله لإبراهيم : لك ذلك ، قد استجبت في إسماعيل ، وإني أبركه وآمنه وأعظمه بما استجبت فيه " . وتفسير هذا الحرف : محمد ﵌ [وفيه أيضا مكتوب : " وأما ابن الأمة فقد باركت عليه جدا جدا] (1) ويلد اثني عشر عظيما ، وأصيره لامة كثيرة " . Among the words of the Torah on this subject, in its first book, are the following. "The angel came down to Abraham and said to him, 'A boy named Isaac will be born to you in this world.' Abraham said, 'Would that Ishmael might live before You in Your service.' God said to Abraham, 'That shall be yours. I have answered you concerning Ishmael. I shall bless him, secure him, and make him great through what I have answered concerning him.'" The interpretation of this word is Muhammad. It is also written in it, "As for the son of the slave woman, I have blessed him exceedingly, exceedingly. He will beget twelve great ones, and I shall make him into a great nation."
The interpretation of the blessing, al-Rawandi says, is Muhammad ﷺ. Majlisi, in the seventeenth century, records that he heard the Hebrew text from People of the Book he trusted.

Al-Suddi's tafsir, quoted in Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 36, p. 216, with Majlisi's own verification, p. 216 انطلق بإسماعيل وأمة حتى تنزله بيت التهامي - يعني مكة - فإني ناشر ذريته وجاعلهم ثقلا على من كفر بي ، وجاعل منهم نبيا عظيما ، ومظهره على الأديان ، وجاعل من ذريته اثني عشر عظيما ، وجاعل ذريته عدد نجوم السماء (5) . أقول : سمعت من جماعة من ثقات أهل الكتاب أنه موجود في توراتهم الآن " وليشمعيل شمعتيك هينه برختي اوتو وهيفريتي اوتو وهيبريتى (6) اوتو بماود ماود شنيم عاسار نسيئيم يوليدو نتيتو لكوى كدول " وسمعتهم يترجمونه هكذا : ومن إسماعيل أسمعتك أني باركت إياه وأوفرت إياه وأكثرت إياه في غاية الغاية اثني عشر رؤساء يولدون ، ووهبته قوما عظيما . Set out with Ishmael and his mother until you bring them down to the house of the Tihamah, meaning Mecca. For I will spread his descendants abroad, make them a burden upon whoever disbelieves in Me, raise from them a great prophet, make him manifest over the religions, make twelve great ones from his descendants, and make his descendants as numerous as the stars of heaven. I say, I heard from a group of trustworthy People of the Book that this is now found in their Torah. "Ule-Yishmael shematikha, hinneh berakhti oto, vehifreti oto vehirbeiti oto bimeod meod, shenem asar nesi'im yolid, netativ legoy gadol." I heard them translate it as follows. "And concerning Ishmael, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, made him fruitful, and multiplied him exceedingly, exceedingly. Twelve chiefs will be born, and I have given him to a great people."

Al-Suddi's tafsir, quoted in Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 36, p. 216, with Majlisi's own verification, continued, p. 216 أقول : الذي يظهر من الاخبار أن " مادماد " اسم محمد ﵌ بالعبرانية I say that what appears from the reports is that "Madmad" is the Hebrew name of Muhammad.

Majlisi transliterates the received text and adds his own view that the blessing's "maddmad," the doubled word of the Hebrew, is the name Muhammad ﵇ in Hebrew. Bihar also carries a longer narrative in which Abraham is shown the twelve in a vision and told they will come forth "from your firstborn Ishmael."

Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 21, pp. 317-318, from Ibn Tawus, Iqbal al-A'mal فقال : رب صلى على محمد وآل محمد ، كما اجتبيتهم وأخلصتهم إخلاصا ، فأوحى ﷿ ليهنئك (1) كرامتي وفضلي عليك ، فإني صائر بسلالة محمد ومن اصطفيت معه منهم إلى قناة صلبك ، ومخرجهم منك ، ثم من بكرك إسماعيل ﵇ ، فأبشر يا إبراهيم فإني واصل صلواتك بصلواتهم ، ومتبع ذلك بركاتي وترحمي عليك وعليهم ، وجاعل حناني (2) وحجتي إلى الأمد المعدود واليوم الموعود الذي أرث فيه سمائي وأرضي ، وأبعث له خلقي بفصل قضائي (3) وإفاضة رحمتي وعدلي . قال : فلما سمع أصحاب رسول الله ﵌ ما أفضى إليه القوم من تلاوة ما تضمنت الجامعة والصحف الدارسة من نعت رسول الله ﵌ وصفة أهل بيته المذكورين معه بما هم به منه وبما شاهدوا من مكانتهم عنده ازداد القوم بذلك يقينا وإيمانا ، واستطيروا له فرحا . قال : ثم صار القوم إلى ما نزل على موسى ﵇ فألفوا في السفر الثاني من التوراة : إني باعث في الأميين من ولد إسماعيل رسولا أنزل عليه كتابي وأبعثه بالشريعة القيمة إلى جميع خلقي ، أوتيه حكمتي ، وأؤيده بملائكتي (4) وجنودي تكون ذريته من ابنة له مباركة باركتها ، ثم من شبلين لها كإسماعيل وإسحاق أصلين لشعبين عظيمين (5) أكثرهم جدا جدا ، يكون منهم اثنا عشر قيما ، أكمل بمحمد ﵌ وبما أرسله به من بلاغ وحكمة ديني وأختم به أنبيائي ورسلي ، فعلى محمد وأمته تقوم الساعة . He said, "My Lord, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You have chosen them and made them wholly sincere." Then the Most High revealed, "Let My honor and My favor upon you give you glad tidings. I shall bring the progeny of Muhammad and those whom I have chosen with him from among them to the channel of your loins. I shall bring them forth from you, then from your firstborn Ishmael. So rejoice, Abraham. I shall join your blessings to their blessings, and I shall follow that with My blessings and My mercy upon you and upon them. I shall make My tenderness and My proof endure until the numbered term and the promised day, when I inherit My heaven and My earth and raise My creatures for the decisive execution of My judgment and the outpouring of My mercy and justice." He said that when the companions of the Messenger of God heard what the people had disclosed by reciting what the comprehensive book and the worn scrolls contained concerning the description of the Messenger of God and the description of his household, who were mentioned with him, concerning what they were to him and what they witnessed of their rank with Him, the people increased thereby in certainty and faith, and their joy over it soared. He said that the people then turned to what had been sent down to Moses. In the second book of the Torah they found, "I shall send among the unlettered people, from the descendants of Ishmael, a messenger upon whom I shall send down My Book. I shall send him with the upright law to all My creatures. I shall give him My wisdom and support him with My angels and My troops. His descendants will be from a blessed daughter whom I have blessed, then from her two cubs, like Ishmael and Isaac, the roots of two great peoples. I shall multiply them exceedingly, exceedingly. Among them will be twelve guardians. Through Muhammad and the message and wisdom with which I send him, I shall complete My religion and seal My prophets and messengers with him. The Hour will come upon Muhammad and his community."

The provenance of that vision is weak. Majlisi takes it from Ibn Tawus, who took it from Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani's book of the mutual imprecation, a compiler known for long unverifiable sirah material. It belongs to the dossier as a report, not as evidence of what Abraham saw.

Classified exactly, this line is a reading of the Torah made by Muslims, resting in its strongest form, al-Nu'mani's, on the dictation of a named Jewish scholar, not on a chain to an Imam. Genesis itself then names the twelve princes as Ishmael's own sons, born in his lifetime (Genesis 25:13-16), and that is the natural historical reading of the promise. The Imami application reads the twelve forward into the nation that came from him instead. After al-Nu'mani and al-Rawandi it becomes a standing argument, carried by al-Hurr al-Amili through al-Bayadi and by later scholars in dozens of volumes. The Bible promises twelve princes from Ishmael. The Islamic corpus counts twelve Imams from Ishmael's greatest descendant. The numerical link is a reasoned reading of Genesis 17:20, and its classical home in the school is the Ghayba of al-Nu'mani.
Twelve Imams in their own reports
The count does not depend on the Bible. The Imami hadith corpus transmits it, and the Tablet of Fatimah ﵍ is its widest report. Al-Kulayni records it in al-Kafi.

Fatimah and Jabir, al-Kafi, vol. 1, pp. 575-576, hadith of the Tablet, p. 575 3 - محمد بن يحيى ومحمد بن عبد الله ، عن عبد الله بن جعفر ، عن الحسن بن ظريف وعلي بن محمد ، عن صالح بن أبي حماد ، عن بكر بن صالح ، عن عبد الرحمن بن سالم ، عن أبي بصير ، عن أبي عبد الله ﵇ قال : قال أبي لجابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري إن لي إليك حاجة فمتى يخف عليك أن أخلو بك فأسألك عنها ، فقال له جابر : أي الأوقات أحببته فخلا به في بعض الأيام فقال له : يا جابر أخبرني عن اللوح الذي رأيته في يد أمي فاطمة ﵍ بنت رسول الله ﵌ وما أخبرتك به أمي أنه في ذلك اللوح مكتوب ؟ فقال جابر : أشهد بالله أني دخلت على أمك فاطمة ﵍ في حياة رسول الله ﵌ فهنيتها بولادة الحسين ورأيت في يديها لوحا أخضر ، ظننت أنه من زمرد ورأيت فيه كتابا أبيض ، شبه لون الشمس ، فقلت لها : بأبي وأمي يا بنت رسول الله ﵌ ما هذا اللوح ؟ فقالت : هذا لوح أهداه الله إلى رسول الله ﵌ فيه اسم أبي واسم بعلي واسم ابني واسم الأوصياء من ولدي وأعطانيه أبي ليبشرني بذلك ، قال جابر فأعطتنيه أمك فاطمة ﵍ فقرأته واستنسخته ، فقال له أبي : فهل لك يا جابر : أن تعرضه علي قال : نعم ، فمشى معه أبي إلى منزل جابر فأخرج صحيفة من رق (1) ، فقال : يا جابر انظر في كتابك لأقرأ [أنا] عليك ، فنظر جابر في نسخته فقرأه أبي فما خالف حرف حرفا ، فقال جابر : فأشهد بالله أني هكذا رأيته في اللوح مكتوبا . بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم هذا كتاب من الله العزيز الحكيم لمحمد نبيه ونوره وسفيره وحجابه ودليله نزل به الروح الأمين من عند رب العالمين ، عظم يا محمد أسمائي واشكر نعمائي ولا تجحد آلائي ، إني أنا الله إله إلا أنا قاصم الجبارين ومديل المظلومين وديان الدين ، إني أنا الله لا إله إلا أنا ، فمن رجا غير فضلي أو خاف غير عدلي ، عذبته عذابا لا أعذبه (2) أحدا من العالمين فإياي فاعبد وعلي فتوكل ، إني لم أبعث نبيا فأكملت أيامه وانقضت مدته إلا جعلت له وصيا وإني فضلتك على الأنبياء وفضلت وصيك على الأوصياء وأكرمتك بشبليك (3) وسبطيك حسن وحسين ، فجعلت حسنا معدن علمي ، Muhammad ibn Yahya and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah narrated from Abd Allah ibn Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Zarif and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Abi Hammad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah, who said My father said to Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, "I have a need to ask of you. When would it be convenient for you for me to be alone with you and ask you about it?" Jabir said to him, "Whenever you wish." One day he was alone with him, and he said, "O Jabir, tell me about the tablet that you saw in the hand of my mother Fatima, daughter of the Messenger of God, and about what my mother told you was written on that tablet." Jabir said, "I bear witness by God that I entered upon your mother Fatima during the lifetime of the Messenger of God and congratulated her on the birth of al-Husayn. I saw in her hands a green tablet, which I thought was made of emerald, and I saw on it white writing, like the color of the sun. I said to her, 'May my father and mother be sacrificed for you, O daughter of the Messenger of God, what is this tablet?' "She said, 'This is a tablet that God gave as a gift to the Messenger of God. It contains the name of my father, the name of my husband, the name of my son, and the names of the trustees from among my descendants. My father gave it to me to bring me glad tidings through it.' "Jabir said, 'Then your mother Fatima gave it to me, and I read it and copied it.' "My father said to him, 'O Jabir, would you show it to me?' "He said, 'Yes.' My father walked with him to Jabir's house, and he brought out a sheet of parchment. He said, 'O Jabir, look at your writing so that I may read it to you.' Jabir looked at his copy, and my father read it. Not one letter differed from another letter. "Jabir said, 'I bear witness by God that this is how I saw it written on the tablet.' In the name of God, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful. This is a writing from God, the Mighty, the Wise, to Muhammad, His prophet, His light, His messenger, His veil, and His guide. The Trustworthy Spirit brought it down from the Lord of the worlds. Magnify My names, O Muhammad. Give thanks for My blessings, and do not deny My favors. I am God. There is no god but I. I crush the tyrants, grant victory to the oppressed, and judge on the Day of Judgment. I am God. There is no god but I. Whoever hopes for other than My grace or fears other than My justice, I will punish with a punishment by which I will punish no one among the worlds. So worship Me and rely upon Me. I did not send a prophet whose days were completed and whose term came to an end without appointing for him a trustee. I favored you above the prophets, favored your trustee above the trustees, and honored you through your two grandsons and descendants, Hasan and Husayn. I made Hasan a repository of My knowledge,

Fatimah and Jabir, al-Kafi, vol. 1, pp. 575-576, hadith of the Tablet, continued, p. 576 بعد انقضاء مدة أبيه وجعلت حسينا خازن وحيي وأكرمته بالشهادة وختمت له بالسعادة ، فهو أفضل من استشهد وأرفع الشهداء درجة ، جعلت كلمتي التامة معه وحجتي البالغة عنده ، بعترته أثيب وأعاقب ، أولهم علي سيد العابدين وزين أوليائي الماضين (1) وابنه شبه جده المحمود محمد الباقر علمي والمعدن لحكمتي سيهلك المرتابون في جعفر ، الراد عليه كالراد علي ، حق القول مني لأكرمن مثوى جعفر ولاسرنه في أشياعه وأنصاره وأوليائه ، أتيحت (2) بعده موسى فتنة عمياء حندس لان خيط فرضي لا ينقطع وحجتي لا تخفى وأن أوليائي يسقون بالكأس الأوفى ، من جحد واحدا منهم فقد جحد نعمتي ومن غير آية من كتابي فقد افترى علي ، ويل للمفترين الجاحدين عند انقضاء مدة موسى عبدي وحبيبي وخيرتي في علي وليي وناصري ومن أضع عليه أعباء النبوة وأمتحنه بالاضطلاع بها يقتله عفريت مستكبر يدفن في المدينة التي بناها العبد الصالح (3) إلى جنب شر خلقي حق القول مني لأسرنه بمحمد ابنه وخليفته من بعده ووارث علمه ، فهو معدن علمي وموضع سري وحجتي على خلقي لا يؤمن عبد به إلا جعلت الجنة مثواه وشفعته في سبعين من أهل بيته كلهم قد استوجبوا النار وأختم بالسعادة لابنه علي وليي وناصري والشاهد في خلقي وأميني علي وحيي ، أخرج منه الداعي إلى سبيلي والخازن لعلمي الحسن وأكمل ذلك بابنه " م ح م د " رحمة للعالمين ، عليه كمال موسى وبهاء عيسى وصبر أيوب فيذل أوليائي في زمانه وتتهادى رؤوسهم كما تتهادى رؤوس الترك والديلم فيقتلون ويحرقون ويكونون خائفين ، مرعوبين ، وجلين ، تصبغ الأرض بدمائهم ويفشو الويل والرنا في نسائهم أولئك أوليائي حقا ، بهم أدفع كل فتنة عمياء حندس وبهم أكشف الزلازل وأدفع الآصار والاغلال أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم ورحمة وأولئك هم المهتدون . قال عبد الرحمن بن سالم : قال أبو بصير : لو لم تسمع في دهرك ، إلا هذا الحديث لكفاك ، فصنه إلا عن أهله . "after his father's term came to an end. I made Husayn the keeper of My revelation. I honored him with martyrdom and sealed his life with happiness. He is the best of those martyred and the martyr of the highest rank. I placed My complete word with him and My conclusive proof with him. Through his progeny I reward and punish. The first of them is Ali, master of the worshippers and adornment of My former saints. His son is the likeness of his praiseworthy grandfather, Muhammad, the splitter open of My knowledge and the mine of My wisdom. Those who doubt concerning Jafar will perish. Whoever rejects him is like one who rejects Me. My word is binding that I will honor Jafar's dwelling place and make him happy through his followers, supporters, and friends. After him Musa will face a blind, dark trial, because the thread of My obligation does not break, My proof is not concealed, and My saints are given the fullest cup to drink. Whoever denies one of them has denied My blessing. Whoever alters a verse of My Book has fabricated a lie against Me. Woe to the lying deniers when the term of Musa, My servant, beloved, and chosen one, comes to an end, concerning Ali, My friend and helper, upon whom I place the burdens of prophethood and whom I test by having him bear them. An arrogant demon will kill him. He will be buried in the city built by the righteous servant, beside the worst of My creatures. My word is binding that I will make him happy through Muhammad, his son, his successor after him, and the heir to his knowledge. He is the repository of My knowledge, the place of My secret, and My proof over My creatures. No servant believes in him without My making Paradise his dwelling place and accepting his intercession for seventy members of his household, all of whom have deserved the Fire. I will seal with happiness his son Ali, My friend and helper, the witness among My creatures, and My trustee over My revelation. From him I will bring forth the caller to My path and the keeper of My knowledge, Hasan. I will complete that through his son Mim Ha Mim Dal, a mercy to the worlds. He will have the perfection of Musa, the splendor of Isa, and the patience of Ayyub. My saints will be humiliated in his time. Their heads will be passed from hand to hand as the heads of the Turks and Daylamites are passed from hand to hand. They will be killed and burned. They will be afraid, terrified, and fearful. The earth will be stained with their blood, and wailing and lamentation will spread among their women. Those are truly My saints. Through them I repel every blind, dark trial. Through them I uncover earthquakes and repel burdens and shackles. Upon them are blessings and mercy from their Lord, and they are the rightly guided." Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim said, "Abu Basir said, 'If you heard nothing in your lifetime except this report, it would be enough for you. So guard it except from those worthy of it.'"

Jabir copied the tablet, and Imam al-Baqir ﵇ read the copy back letter for letter. Its text names the twelve in order, from Ali ﵇ the trustee through al-Hasan ﵇ and al-Husayn ﵇ to "Mim Ha Mim Dal, a mercy to the worlds," the awaited one. Al-Saduq carries the Tablet in Kamal al-Din and Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, al-Tusi in his Ghayba and his Amali, and al-Khazzaz in al-Kifaya, through chains that differ and converge on Jabir.
Beside the Tablet, the count is stated in plain words and preserved in five cited works, Kamal al-Din, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, Ithbat al-Hudat, and Bihar al-Anwar among them.

The Prophet, Kamal al-Din, p. 289, carried also by Uyun al-Akhbar, Ithbat al-Hudat, and Bihar 4 - حدثنا علي بن أحمد ﵁ قال : حدثنا محمد بن أبي عبد الله الكوفي عن موسى بن عمران ، عن عمه الحسين بن يزيد ، عن الحسن بن علي بن أبي حمزة ، عن أبيه ، عن يحيى بن أبي القاسم ، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد ، عن أبيه ، عن جده ﵈ قال : قال رسول الله ﵌ : الأئمة بعدي اثنا عشر أولهم علي بن أبي طالب وآخرهم القائم ، هم خلفائي وأوصيائي وأوليائي ، وحجج الله على أمتي بعدي ، المقر بهم مؤمن ، والمنكر لهم كافر (2) . Ali ibn Ahmad narrated to us. He said that Muhammad ibn Abi Abd Allah al-Kufi narrated to us from Musa ibn Imran, from his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from his father, from Yahya ibn Abi al-Qasim, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said The Messenger of God said, "The Imams after me are twelve. The first of them is Ali ibn Abi Talib, and the last of them is al-Qa'im. They are my successors, my trustees, my friends, and God's proofs against my community after me. Whoever acknowledges them is a believer, and whoever denies them is an unbeliever."
Kamal al-Din, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, Ithbat al-Hudat, and Bihar al-Anwar all carry it, and al-Hurr al-Amili notes that al-Khazzaz carried it from Ibn Babawayh with the same chain.
The Tradition also ties its twelve to Israel's twelve, in a report whose Sunni chains al-Saduq deliberately records.

Al-Saduq, Kamal al-Din, pp. 97-98, Sunni-chained reports and his verdict عهد إلينا نبينا ﵌ أنه يكون من بعده اثنا عشر خليفة بعدد نقباء بني إسرائيل . وقد أخرجت بعض طرق هذا الحديث في هذا الكتاب وبعضها في كتاب النص على الأئمة الاثني عشر ﵈ . بالإمامة . ونقل مخالفونا من أصحاب الحديث نقلا ظاهرا مستفيضا من حديث جابر بن سمرة ما حدثنا به أحمد بن محمد بن إسحاق الدينوري ، وكان من أصحاب الحديث قال : حدثني أبو بكر بن أبي داود (1) ، عن إسحاق بن إبراهيم ابن شاذان ، عن الوليد بن هشام ، عن محمد بن ذكوان (2) قال : حدثني أبي ، عن أبيه ، عن ابن سيرين ، عن جابر بن سمرة السوائي قال : كنا عند النبي ﵌ فقال : يلي هذه الأمة اثنا عشر ، قال : فصرخ الناس فلم أسمع ما قال : فقلت لأبي - وكان أقرب إلى رسول الله ﵌ مني : ما قال : رسول الله ﵌ ؟ فقال : قال : كلهم من قريش وكلهم لا يرى مثله . وقد أخرجت طرق هذا الحديث أيضا ، وبعضهم روى " اثنا عشر أميرا " ، وبعضهم روى " اثنا عشر خليفة " فدل ذلك على أن الاخبار التي في يد الامامية ، عن النبي ﵌ والأئمة ﵈ بذكر الأئمة الاثني عشر أخبار صحيحة (3) . Our Prophet entrusted us that after him there would be twelve caliphs, equal in number to the nuqaba of the Children of Israel. I have presented some of the chains of this report in this book and some in the book on the designation of the twelve Imams to the Imamate. Our opponents among the traditionists have transmitted widely and openly the report of Jabir ibn Samurah. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Dinawari, who was among the traditionists, narrated to us that Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud narrated to him from Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan, from al-Walid ibn Hisham, from Muhammad ibn Dhakwan, who said that his father narrated to him from his father, from Ibn Sirin, from Jabir ibn Samurah al-Suwa'i, who said We were with the Prophet when he said, "Twelve will rule this community." The people cried out, and I did not hear what he said. I said to my father, who was closer to the Messenger of God than I was, "What did the Messenger of God say?" He said, "He said that all of them are from Quraysh, and none of them will be seen to have his like." I have also presented the chains of this report. Some of them narrated "twelve commanders," and some narrated "twelve caliphs." This indicates that the reports held by the Imamiyya from the Prophet and the Imams concerning the mention of the twelve Imams are sound reports.

Saduq's opening report ties the count to the nuqaba, the twelve tribal chiefs Moses appointed, one from each tribe, when the land was first scouted. The opponents' own widespread reports validate the Imami reports about the twelve Imams, as al-Saduq argues, and al-Kafi carries the comparison with the twelve trustees of Isa ﵇.

Imam al-Baqir, al-Kafi, vol. 1, p. 580 10 - علي بن إبراهيم ، عن محمد بن عيسى بن عبيد ، عن محمد بن الفضيل ، عن أبي حمزة ، عن أبي جعفر ﵇ قال : إن الله أرسل محمدا ﵌ إلى الجن والإنس وجعل من بعده اثني عشر وصيا ، منهم من سبق ومنهم من بقي وكل وصي جرت به سنة والأوصياء الذين من بعد محمد ﵌ على سنة أوصياء عيسى وكانوا اثني عشر وكان أمير المؤمنين ﵇ على سنة المسيح . Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Jafar, who said, "Allah sent Muhammad to the jinn and humankind, and after him He appointed twelve trustees. Some of them have passed and some remain. Each trustee has had a pattern run through him. The trustees after Muhammad follow the pattern of the trustees of Jesus. They were twelve, and the Commander of the Faithful followed the pattern of the Messiah."

The trustees after Muhammad ﷺ run on the pattern of the trustees of Jesus ﵇, and they were twelve. The stranger in the Sacred Mosque who testifies to each Imam by name in sequence, whom Ali ﵇ identifies as al-Khidr, completes the series in al-Kafi's own chapter.

Al-Hasan answering, al-Kafi, vol. 1, pp. 573-574 فالتفت أمير المؤمنين ﵇ إلى الحسن فقال : يا أبا محمد أجبه ، قال : فأجابه الحسن ﵇ فقال الرجل أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله ولم أزل أشهد بها وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله ولم أزل أشهد بذلك وأشهد أنك وصي رسول الله ﵌ والقائم بحجته - وأشار إلى أمير المؤمنين - ولم أزل أشهد بها وأشهد أنك وصيه والقائم بحجته - وأشار إلى الحسن ﵇ - وأشهد أن الحسين بن علي وصي أخيه والقائم بحجته بعده وأشهد على علي بن الحسين أنه القائم بأمر الحسين بعده وأشهد على محمد بن علي أنه القائم بأمر علي بن الحسين وأشهد على جعفر بن محمد بأنه القائم بأمر محمد وأشهد على موسى أنه القائم بأمر جعفر بن محمد وأشهد على علي بن موسى أنه القائم بأمر موسى بن جعفر وأشهد على محمد بن علي أنه القائم بأمر علي ابن موسى وأشهد على علي بن محمد بأنه القائم بأمر محمد بن علي وأشهد على الحسن بن علي بأنه القائم بأمر علي بن محمد وأشهد على رجل من ولد الحسن لا يكنى ولا يسمى حتى يظهر أمره فيملاها عدلا كما ملئت جورا والسلام عليك يا أمير المؤمنين ورحمة الله وبركاته ، ثم قام فمضى ، فقال أمير المؤمنين : يا أبا محمد اتبعه فانظر أين يقصد فخرج الحسن بن علي ﵉ فقال : ما كان إلا أن وضع رجله خارجا من المسجد فما دريت أين أخذ من أرض الله ، فرجعت إلى أمير المؤمنين ﵇ فأعلمته ، فقال : يا أبا محمد أتعرفه ؟ قلت : الله ورسوله وأمير المؤمنين أعلم ، قال : هو الخضر ﵇ . The Commander of the Faithful turned to al-Hasan and said, "O Abu Muhammad, answer him." Al-Hasan answered him. The man said, "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I have never ceased to bear witness to it. I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and I have never ceased to bear witness to that. I bear witness that you are the trustee of the Messenger of Allah and the one who upholds his proof," and he pointed to the Commander of the Faithful. "I have never ceased to bear witness to it. I bear witness that you are his trustee and the one who upholds his proof," and he pointed to al-Hasan. "I bear witness that al-Husayn ibn Ali is the trustee of his brother and the one who upholds his proof after him. I bear witness concerning Ali ibn al-Husayn that he is the one who upholds the affair of al-Husayn after him. I bear witness concerning Muhammad ibn Ali that he is the one who upholds the affair of Ali ibn al-Husayn. I bear witness concerning Jafar ibn Muhammad that he is the one who upholds the affair of Muhammad. I bear witness concerning Musa that he is the one who upholds the affair of Jafar ibn Muhammad. I bear witness concerning Ali ibn Musa that he is the one who upholds the affair of Musa ibn Jafar. I bear witness concerning Muhammad ibn Ali that he is the one who upholds the affair of Ali ibn Musa. I bear witness concerning Ali ibn Muhammad that he is the one who upholds the affair of Muhammad ibn Ali. I bear witness concerning al-Hasan ibn Ali that he is the one who upholds the affair of Ali ibn Muhammad. I bear witness concerning a man from the descendants of al-Hasan, who is neither given a kunyah nor named until his affair appears, and he will fill it with justice as it has been filled with tyranny. Peace be upon you, Commander of the Faithful, and Allah's mercy and blessings." Then he rose and left. The Commander of the Faithful said, "O Abu Muhammad, follow him and see where he is going." Al-Hasan ibn Ali went out and said, "As soon as he put his foot outside the mosque, I did not know where in Allah's earth he had gone." I returned to the Commander of the Faithful and informed him. He said, "O Abu Muhammad, do you know him?" I said, "Allah, His Messenger, and the Commander of the Faithful know best." He said, "He is al-Khidr."

The last of the twelve is "a man from the descendants of al-Hasan, who is neither given a kunyah nor named until his affair appears, and he will fill it with justice as it has been filled with tyranny." A kunyah is an honorific byname, Abu so-and-so, and the report's point is that the twelfth one is publicly no one at all until he rises.
Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon
The Sunni collections carry the number with chains their own scholars grade highly. Sahih Muslim transmits the report of Jabir ibn Samura through a cluster of chains.

The Prophet, Sahih Muslim, Kitab al-Imara, Jabir ibn Samura's reports حدثنا قتيبة بن سعيد حدثنا جرير عن حصين عن جابر بن سمرة قال سمعت النبي ﵌ يقول ح وحدثنا رفاعة بن الهيثم الواسطي (واللفظ له) حدثنا خالد (يعنى ابن عبد الله الطحان) عن حصين عن جابر بن سمرة قال دخلت مع أبي على النبي ﵌ فسمعته يقول إن هذا الامر لا ينقضي حتى يمضى فيهم اثنا عشر خليفة قال ثم تكلم بكلام خفى على قال فقلت لأبي ما قال قال كلهم من قريش حدثنا ابن أبي عمر حدثنا سفيان عن عبد الملك بن عمير عن جابر بن سمرة قال سمعت النبي ﵌ يقول لا يزال امر الناس ماضيا ما وليهم اثنا عشر رجلا ثم تكلم النبي ﷺ بكلمة خفيت على فسألت أبى ماذا قال رسول الله ﷺ فقال كلهم من قريش Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us. Jarir narrated to us from Husayn, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said, "I heard the Prophet say." It was also narrated to us by Rifa'ah ibn al-Haytham al-Wasiti, and this is his wording. Khalid, meaning Ibn Abd Allah al-Tahhan, narrated to us from Husayn, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said, "I entered with my father upon the Prophet, and I heard him say, 'This matter will not end until twelve caliphs have passed among them.' He then spoke words that were indistinct to me. I said to my father, 'What did he say?' He said, 'All of them are from Quraysh.'" Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us. Sufyan narrated to us from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said, "I heard the Prophet say, 'The affairs of the people will continue as long as twelve men rule them.' Then the Prophet spoke a word that was indistinct to me, so I asked my father, 'What did the Messenger of God say?' He said, 'All of them are from Quraysh.'"
The Musnad of Ahmad carries the parallel that matters most for the Bible question, in the report of Masruq.

Ibn Mas'ud's report, Musnad Ahmad, vol. 1, p. 398 (33) حدثنا عبد اللّه ، حدثني أبي ، ثنا حسن بن موسى ، ثنا حماد بن زيد عن المجالد ، عن الشعبي ، عن مسروق ، قال : كنا جلوسا عند عبد اللّه بن مسعود ، - وهو يقرئنا القرآن - ، فقال له رجل : يا أبا عبد الرحمن هل سألتم رسول اللّه ﵆ كم تملك هذه الأمة من خليفة ؟ فقال عبد اللّه بن مسعود : ما سألني عنها أحد منذ قدمت العراق قبلك ، ثم قال : نعم ، ولقد سألنا رسول اللّه ﵆ فقال : اثنا عشر ، كعدّة نقباء (1) بني إسرائيل . 1 / 398 (33) Abd Allah told us. My father told me. Hasan ibn Musa told us. Hammad ibn Zayd told us, from Mujalid, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said We were sitting with Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud while he was teaching us the Quran. A man said to him, "Abu Abd al-Rahman, did you ask the Messenger of God how many caliphs will rule this community?" Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said, "No one has asked me about it before you since I came to Iraq." Then he said, "Yes, we did ask the Messenger of God, and he said, 'Twelve, equal to the number of the nuqaba of the Children of Israel.'" Musnad, volume 1, page 398
The Sunan of Abu Dawud devotes a chapter to the Mahdi and gives the reports their form.

(4282) Musaddad narrated to us that Umar ibn Ubayd narrated to them. Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us. Abu Bakr, meaning Ibn Ayyash, narrated to us. Musaddad narrated to us. Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us. Za'idah informed us. Ahmad ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to me, from Fitr. The meaning is one. All of them narrated from Asim, from Zirr, from Abd Allah, from the Prophet, who said, "Even if only one day remained of this world," Za'idah said in his report, "Allah would lengthen that day," then they agreed, "until He sends in it a man from me or from my Household, whose name corresponds to my name and whose father's name corresponds to my father's name." Fitr added in his report, "He will fill the earth with equity and justice as it has been filled with oppression and tyranny." Sufyan said in his report, "The world will not pass away, or will not come to an end, until a man from my Household whose name corresponds to my name rules the Arabs." Abu Dawud said, "The wording of Umar and Abu Bakr has the same meaning as that of Sufyan."

One clause of this report, "and whose father's name corresponds to my father's name," is absent from Ibn Hanbal's transmissions of the same report, and al-Kanji al-Shafi'i, who collected the Mahdi reports in the seventh century, noted the absence, recorded the harmonizations proposed to keep the clause, and dismissed them as forced. The clause is the one obstacle to reading the report of the twelfth Imam, whose father was al-Hasan ﵇ and not Abdullah, and it is precisely the clause the strongest chains do not carry.
The Sunni commentary tradition itself records the problem.

Al-Nawawi, Sharh Sahih Muslim, vol. 12, pp. 200-201 قوله (﵌) (أن هذا الأمر لا ينقضي حتى يمضي فيهم اثنا عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش) وفي رواية لا يزال أمر الناس ماضيا ما وليهم اثنا عشر رجلا كلهم من قريش [وفي رواية لا يزال الإسلام عزيزا إلى اثنى عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش قال القاضي قد توجه هنا سؤالان أحدهما أنه قد جاء في الحديث الآخر الخلافة بعدي ثلاثون سنة ثم تكون ملكا وهذا مخالف لحديث اثنى عشر خليفة فإنه لم يكن في ثلاثين سنة إلا الخلفاء الراشدون الأربعة والأشهر التي بويع فيها الحسن بن علي قال والجواب عن هذا أن المراد في حديث الخلافة ثلاثون سنة خلافة النبوة وقد جاء مفسرا في بعض الروايات خلافة النبوة بعدي ثلاثون سنة ثم تكون ملكا ولم يشترط هذا في الاثني عشر السؤال الثاني أنه قد ولى أكثر من هذا العدد قال وهذا اعتراض باطل لأنه (﵌) لم يقل لا يلي إلا اثنى عشر خليفة وإنما قال يلي وقد ولي هذا العدد ولا يضر كونه وجد بعدهم غيرهم His statement, "This matter will not end until twelve caliphs have passed among them, all of them from Quraysh." In one version, "The affairs of the people will continue as long as twelve men rule them, all of them from Quraysh." In another version, "Islam will remain mighty until twelve caliphs, all of them from Quraysh." Al-Qadi said that two questions arise here. The first is that another report states, "The caliphate after me will last thirty years, then there will be kingship." This conflicts with the report of twelve caliphs, for within thirty years there were only the four Rightly Guided Caliphs and the months during which Hasan ibn Ali received allegiance. He said that the answer is that the caliphate meant in the report of thirty years is the caliphate of prophethood. This is explained in some versions, "The caliphate of prophethood after me will last thirty years, then there will be kingship." This was not stipulated regarding the twelve. The second question is that more than this number have ruled. He said that this objection is invalid, because he did not say that only twelve caliphs would rule. Rather, he said that they would rule. This number has ruled, and it does not matter that others were found after them.

Al-Nawawi records the two objections, the thirty-year caliphate report and the plain fact that more than twelve have ruled, and gives al-Qadi Iyad's answers, that the thirty years are the caliphate of prophethood while the twelve carry no such condition, and that the Prophet said twelve would rule, not that only twelve would rule, so the count was already completed and the later rulers do not harm it. The second answer turns the prophecy into a tally of rulers already past. One Sunni voice in Kanz al-Ummal read the whole set as past history, twelve commanders then the Hour, and was corrected by Ibn Abbas himself, as the entry records, that after the twelve come al-Mansur, al-Saffah, and the Mahdi who hands the affair to Isa ﵇.

Ibn Abbas's rebuke, Kanz al-Ummal, vol. 14, entry 39657 39657 عن سعيد بن جبير قال : سمعنا ابن عباس ونحن نقول : اثنا عشر أميرا ثم لا أمير ، واثنا عشر أميرا ثم هي الساعة ، فقال : ما أحمقكم ! إن منا أهل البيت بعد ذلك : المنصور والسفاح والمهدي يدفعها إلى عيسى ابن مريم (كر) . Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, "We heard Ibn Abbas while we were saying, 'Twelve commanders, then no commander. Twelve commanders, then the Hour.' He said, 'How foolish you are. After that, among us, the people of the House, are al-Mansur, al-Saffah, and al-Mahdi. He will hand it over to Jesus son of Mary.'"
That report reads the Mahdi as an Abbasid caliph, and it is counterevidence of a kind. It shows one reader in the Sunni corpus pressing the number onto the rulers he knew.

The Bible's end-time king is described across Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, the Psalms, and Daniel.

John 18:36, Textus Receptus, Van Dyck, King James Version, continued ليست من هذا العالم . لو كانت مملكتي من هذا العالم لكان خدامي يجاهدون لكي لا أسلم إلى اليهود . ولكن الآن ليست مملكتي من هنا apekrithē Iēsous, hē basileia hē emē ouk estin ek tou kosmou toutou. ei ek tou kosmou toutou ēn hē basileia hē emē, hoi hypēretai an hoi emoi ēgōnizonto hina mē paradothō tois Ioudaiois. nyn de hē basileia hē emē ouk estin enteuthen. "Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence."

Jesus ﵇ before Pilate declines an earthly kingdom. The nations did not stream to Zion's law, the swords did not become plowshares, the dispersed were not gathered under one Davidic shepherd, and Rome was not broken and replaced. The standard Christian answer is that the promises await the second coming, and that answer confirms the essential point. They were not fulfilled by the first advent.

These texts do not logically eliminate the Christian claim that Jesus ﵇ himself returns and performs them. What they eliminate is the claim that they were already fulfilled in the ministry of Jesus of Nazareth. Once the Christian places the fulfillment in the future, the dispute changes its shape. It is no longer whether the prophecies await a future just ruler. It is who that ruler is, and whether the returning Isa ﵇ is himself the king or stands behind another.

Against that job description the Islamic corpus names a candidate, from the Prophet's ﷺ own house, from Fatimah's ﵍ children.

Umm Salama and Abu Sa'id, Sunan Abi Dawud, vol. 4, p. 176, reports 4284-4285 قَالَتْ : سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ : « الْمَهْدِيُّ مِنْ عِتْرَتِي مِنْ وَلَدِ فَاطِمَةَ » . قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ : وَسَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْمَلِيحِ ، يُثْنِي عَلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ نُفَيْلٍ وَيَذْكُرُ مِنْهُ صَلَاحًا . Abd Allah ibn Jafar said, "I heard Abu al-Malih praise Ali ibn Nufayl and mention his righteousness." (4285) Sahl ibn Tammam ibn Bazi narrated to us. Ibn al-Munadi's al-Malahim, a Sunni book of the end times, carries the fullest form of the reign.

Abu Sa'id's report, Ibn al-Munadi, al-Malahim, p. 188 الحسن ، عن العلاء بن بشير (1) ، عن أبي الصديق الناجي ، عن أبي سعيد الخدري ، عن النبيّ ﵌ أنّه قال : أبشروا بالمهدي ، رجل من عترتي ، يخرج في اختلاف من الناس وزلازل ، فيملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا ، كما ملئت جورا وظلما ، ويرضى عنه ساكن السماء ، وساكن الأرض ، ويقسم المال صحاحا (2) . قالوا : وما صحاحا ؟ قالوا : بالسويّة ، ويملأ اللّه قلوب امّة محمّد ﵌ غناء ، ويسعهم عدله ، حتّى أنّه ليأمر مناديه فينادي : من له إلى مال حاجة ؟ فما يأتيه أحد ، إلّا رجل واحد ، يأتيه فيسأله ، فيقول له : انطلق إلى السادن ، حتّى يعطيك . قال : فيأتيه فيقول له : أنا رسول المهديّ ، لتعطيني مالا ، فيقول له : احث (3) ، فيحثي فلا يستطيع أن يحمله ، فيلقي حتّى يكون قدر ما يستطيع حمله ، فيخرج به ، فيندم . فيقول : إذا ، كنت أجشع امّة محمّد نفسا ، دعتني إلى هذا المال ، وقد تركه غيري ، قال : فيرجع ، فيردّه عليه ، فيقول له : هذا المال لا نقبل منه شيئا ، اعطيناكه . قال : فيلبث بذلك سبعا ، [ أو ] ثمانيا ، [ أو ] تسع سنين (4) ، كذلك لا خير في الحياة بعده (5) . Al-Hasan, from al-Ala ibn Bashir (1), from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said, "Receive glad tidings of the Mahdi, a man from my progeny. He will emerge amid disagreement among people and earthquakes. He will fill the earth with equity and justice as it has been filled with injustice and oppression. The inhabitant of heaven and the inhabitant of earth will be pleased with him, and he will distribute wealth in full portions (2)." They said, "What does 'in full portions' mean?" He said, "Equally." God will fill the hearts of Muhammad's community with sufficiency, and his justice will encompass them, so much so that he will order his caller to proclaim, "Who has need of wealth?" No one will come to him except one man. He will come and ask him, and he will say to him, "Go to the keeper, so that he may give you." He said, "He will go to him and say, 'I am the Mahdi's messenger, so give me wealth.' He will say to him, 'Take a handful' (3). He will take a handful, but will not be able to carry it. So he will put back enough that he can carry, then leave with it and regret it. He will say, 'Then I am the most covetous soul in Muhammad's community. This wealth called me, while others left it.' He will return and give it back to him, but he will say, 'We do not accept anything back from this wealth. We gave it to you.'" He will remain thus for seven, or eight, or nine years (4). There is no good in life after it (5).

The correspondence with the seventy-second psalm's king is functional. That king judges the poor and the needy, breaks the oppressor, and has dominion from sea to sea. Isaiah's ruler judges the poor with righteousness. The Prophet's ﷺ report makes the Mahdi the one who reverses an earth filled with injustice. The Bible's king brings abundance and peace while the moon endures. The Mahdi's reign fills hearts with sufficiency and empties the treasury of petitioners.
The distinction that matters is the one the reports draw themselves. The returning Isa ﵇ is present, and another is the imam.

Abu Hurayra's report, Musnad Ahmad, vol. 2, p. 336 (97) حدثنا عبد اللّه ، حدثني أبي ، ثنا عثمان بن عمر ، ثنا ابن أبي ذئب ، عن الزهري ، عن نافع - مولى أبي قتادة - ، عن أبي هريرة : ان النبي ﵆ قال : كيف بكم إذا نزل فيكم عيسى بن مريم وامامكم منكم . 2 / 336 (97) Abdullah narrated to us.
